title.zh: 卷七十三 志第四十九 職官二
title.raw: 卷七十三 志第四十九 職官二 Volume 73 Treatises 49: Official Posts 2

sentences.zh: 都察院 附總督 巡撫

translations.literal: Censorate; appended: Governors-General, Grand Coordinators
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate; with appended sections on Governors-General and Grand Coordinators

sentences.zh: 都察院。

translations.literal: The Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate.

sentences.zh: 左、右都御史，正二品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Censors-in-Chief, rank 2a;
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Censors-in-Chief, rank 2a;

sentences.zh: 左、右副都御史，正三品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Censors-in-Chief, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Vice Censors-in-Chief, rank 3a;

sentences.zh: 左、右僉都御史，正四品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistant Censors-in-Chief, rank 4a.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Assistant Censors-in-Chief, rank 4a.

sentences.zh: 其屬，經歷司，經歷一人，正六品；

translations.literal: Its subordinate offices: the Registry, with one Registrar, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate offices included a Registry with one Registrar at rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 都事一人，正七品；

translations.literal: one Secretariat Clerk, rank 7a;
translations.idiomatic: one Secretariat Clerk at rank 7a;

sentences.zh: 司務廳，司務二人，從九品，初設四人，後革二人；

translations.literal: the Clerks Office, two Clerks, rank 9b; initially four were appointed, later two were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: a Clerks Office with two Clerks at rank 9b (initially four, later reduced by two);

sentences.zh: 照磨所，照磨，正八品；

translations.literal: the Copying Office, one Copying Clerk, rank 8a;
translations.idiomatic: a Copying Office with one Copying Clerk at rank 8a;

sentences.zh: 檢校，正九品；

translations.literal: one Reviser, rank 9a;
translations.idiomatic: one Reviser at rank 9a;

sentences.zh: 司獄司，司獄，從九品，初設六人，後革五人；

translations.literal: the Prison Office, one Prison Superintendent, rank 9b; initially six were appointed, later five were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: a Prison Office with one Prison Superintendent at rank 9b (initially six, later reduced to one);

sentences.zh: 各一人。

translations.literal: one each.
translations.idiomatic: one post in each case.

sentences.zh: 十三道監察御史一百十人，正七品。

translations.literal: One hundred and ten Investigating Censors in the thirteen circuits, rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred and ten Investigating Censors across thirteen circuits, all at rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 浙江、江西、河南、山東各十人，福建、廣東、廣西、四川、貴州各七人，陝西、湖廣、山西各八人，雲南十一人。

translations.literal: Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Henan, and Shandong had ten each; Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, and Guizhou had seven each; Shaanxi, Huguang, and Shanxi had eight each; Yunnan had eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Henan, and Shandong each had ten; Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, and Guizhou each had seven; Shaanxi, Huguang, and Shanxi each had eight; Yunnan had eleven.

sentences.zh: 其在外加都御史或副、僉都御史銜者，有總督，有提督，有巡撫，有總督兼巡撫，提督兼巡撫，及經略、總理、贊理、巡視、撫治等員。

translations.literal: Those serving outside with the additional title of Censor-in-Chief or Vice or Assistant Censor-in-Chief included Governors-General, Military Supervisors, Grand Coordinators, Governors-General also serving as Grand Coordinators, Military Supervisors also serving as Grand Coordinators, and commissioners for military pacification, overall supervision, assistance in management, inspection, and pacification administration.
translations.idiomatic: Officials posted outside with added ranks as Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor-in-Chief, or Assistant Censor-in-Chief served as Governors-General, Military Supervisors, Grand Coordinators, or combined posts; other titles included Pacification Commissioner, Overall Supervisor, Assistant Supervisor, Inspector, and Pacification Administrator.

sentences.zh: 巡撫之名，起於懿文太子巡撫陝西。

translations.literal: The title Grand Coordinator originated when the heir apparent Yiwen pacified Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The title Grand Coordinator dates to when the heir apparent Yiwen served as coordinator in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年，遣尚書蹇義等二十六人巡行天下，安撫軍民。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle, twenty-six men including Minister Jian Yi were dispatched to tour the realm and reassure troops and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 19 (1421), twenty-six officials led by Minister Jian Yi were sent to tour the empire and reassure soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 以後不拘尚書、侍郎、都御史、少卿等官。

translations.literal: Thereafter no restriction was made to Ministers, Vice Ministers, Censors-in-Chief, or Junior Chamberlains and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the post was not limited to ministers, vice ministers, censors-in-chief, or junior chamberlains.

sentences.zh: 事畢復命，即或停遣。

translations.literal: When the task was finished they reported back; dispatch might then cease.
translations.idiomatic: When their mission ended they returned to report, and the appointment might then lapse.

sentences.zh: 初名巡撫，或名鎮守，後以鎮守侍郎與巡按御史不相統屬，文移窒礙，定為都御史。

translations.literal: At first the title was Grand Coordinator, or sometimes Garrison Commander; later, because the Garrison Commander Vice Minister and the Touring Investigating Censor were not in the same chain of command and documents were obstructed, the post was fixed as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The post was first called Grand Coordinator or sometimes Garrison Commander; because the garrison vice minister and the touring investigating censor did not share a single chain of command and paperwork stalled, the title was fixed as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 巡撫兼軍務者加提督，有總兵地方加贊理或參贊，所轄多、事重者加總督。

translations.literal: A Grand Coordinator who also handled military affairs received the additional title Military Supervisor; where there was a regional commander, Assistant Supervisor or Participating Supervisor was added; where jurisdiction was broad and affairs weighty, Governor-General was added.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinators who also handled military affairs took the added title Military Supervisor; regions with regional commanders added Assistant or Participating Supervisor; broad jurisdictions with heavy responsibilities added Governor-General.

sentences.zh: 他如整飭、撫治、巡治、總理等項，皆因事特設。

translations.literal: Other titles such as Rectification, Pacification Administration, Touring Administration, and Overall Supervision were all established ad hoc according to the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Other titles—Rectification, Pacification Administration, Touring Administration, Overall Supervision—were all created ad hoc as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 其以尚書、侍郎任總督軍務者，皆兼都御史，以便行事。

translations.literal: Those who as Minister or Vice Minister bore responsibility for overall military affairs all concurrently held the title Censor-in-Chief, to facilitate their conduct of business.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers or vice ministers appointed to overall military command all concurrently held the rank of Censor-in-Chief so they could act effectively.

sentences.zh: 都御史，職專糾劾百司，辯明冤枉，提督各道，為天子耳目風紀之司。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief was charged exclusively with impeaching the hundred offices, clarifying wrongful accusations, supervising all circuits, and serving as the Son of Heaven's bureau of eyes, ears, and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief impeached officials across the bureaucracy, cleared wrongful charges, supervised all censor circuits, and served as the emperor's eyes, ears, and guardian of discipline.

sentences.zh: 凡大臣奸邪、小人構黨、作威福亂政者，劾。

translations.literal: All great ministers who were treacherous and wicked, petty men who formed factions, or those who wielded authority and blessings to disturb government—impeach.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached great ministers who were treacherous, petty men who formed factions, and anyone who abused power to disrupt government.

sentences.zh: 凡百官猥茸貪冒壞官紀者，劾。

translations.literal: All officials of the hundred offices who were base, greedy, and corrupt and who ruined official discipline—impeach.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached officials who were base, greedy, and corrupt and who undermined official discipline.

sentences.zh: 凡學術不正、上書陳言變亂成憲、希進用者，劾。

translations.literal: All whose learning was unsound, who submitted memorials proposing to alter established statutes, or who hoped for advancement through such means—impeach.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached those whose scholarship was unsound, who memorialized to overturn established law, or who sought advancement by such means.

sentences.zh: 遇朝覲、考察，同吏部司賢否陟黜。

translations.literal: On occasions of court audience and performance review, together with the Ministry of Personnel he judged merit and demerit for promotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: At court audiences and performance reviews he worked with the Ministry of Personnel to judge officials for promotion or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 大獄重囚會鞫於外朝，偕刑部、大理讞平之。

translations.literal: Major cases and serious prisoners were jointly tried in the outer court; together with the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review he deliberated and settled verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: Major trials and serious prisoners were heard in the outer court; together with the Ministry of Justice and the Court of Judicial Review he settled verdicts.

sentences.zh: 其奉敕內地，拊循外地，各專其敕行事。

translations.literal: Those who received imperial orders for the interior pacified and comforted the interior; those for the exterior each acted solely according to their commission.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners for the interior pacified the heartland; those for the exterior each acted solely under their commission.

sentences.zh: 十三道監察御史，主察糾內外百司之官邪，或露章面劾，或封章奏劾。

translations.literal: The Investigating Censors of the thirteen circuits were chiefly charged with investigating and impeaching misconduct among officials within and without the hundred offices, whether by open memorial and face-to-face impeachment or by sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censors of the thirteen circuits investigated misconduct among officials throughout the bureaucracy, impeaching either by open memorial in court or by sealed memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 在內兩京刷卷，巡視京營，監臨鄉、會試及武舉，巡視光祿，巡視倉場，巡視內庫、皇城、五城，輪值登聞鼓。

translations.literal: Within the capital they reviewed case files in both capitals, inspected the capital garrisons, supervised the provincial and metropolitan civil examinations and the military examination, inspected the Court of Imperial Entertainments, inspected granaries, inspected the inner treasuries, the Imperial City, and the Five Wards, and took turns at the Petition Drum.
translations.idiomatic: In the capitals they reviewed judicial files, inspected capital garrisons, supervised civil and military examinations, inspected the Court of Imperial Entertainments and granaries, inspected inner treasuries, the Imperial City, and the Five Wards, and took turns at the Petition Drum.

sentences.zh: 後改科員。

translations.literal: Later this was changed to staff of the Six Offices of Scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Later these duties passed to the Six Offices of Scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 在外巡按，北直隸二人，南直隸三人，宣大一人，遼東一人，甘肅一人，十三省各一人。

translations.literal: Outside the capital for touring inspection: two for North Zhili, three for South Zhili, one for Xuanhua-Datong, one for Liaodong, one for Gansu, and one for each of the thirteen provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital for touring inspection: North Zhili had two, South Zhili three, Xuanhua-Datong one, Liaodong one, Gansu one, and each of the thirteen provinces one.

sentences.zh: 清軍，提督學校，兩京各一人，萬曆末，南京增設一人。

translations.literal: For troop muster review and supervision of schools, one each in both capitals; at the end of the Wanli reign one additional post was added in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Troop muster review and school supervision had one censor each in both capitals; at the end of Wanli Nanjing gained an additional post.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽，兩淮一人，兩浙一人，長蘆一人，河東一人。

translations.literal: For salt inspection: one for Liang-Huai, one for Liang-Zhe, one for Changlu, one for Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Salt inspection: one each for Liang-Huai, Liang-Zhe, Changlu, and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 茶馬，陝西。

translations.literal: For tea-and-horse trade: Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tea-and-horse trade: Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 巡漕，巡關，宣德四年設立鈔關御史，至正統十年始遣主事。

translations.literal: Grain transport inspection, customs inspection; in the fourth year of Xuande a Censor for paper-tax customs was established, but not until the tenth year of Zhengtong were Directors dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport and customs inspection; in Xuande year 4 a censor for paper-tax customs was established, but not until Zhengtong year 10 were directors dispatched instead.

sentences.zh: 攢運，印馬，屯田。

translations.literal: Grain consolidation transport, horse branding, and garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: Grain consolidation transport, horse branding, and garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 師行則監軍紀功，各以其事專監察。

translations.literal: When armies marched they supervised military discipline and recorded merit; each according to his charge conducted specialized oversight.
translations.idiomatic: When armies marched they supervised discipline and recorded merit; each censor oversaw his assigned specialty.

sentences.zh: 而巡按則代天子巡狩，所按籓服大臣、府州縣官諸考察，舉劾尤專，大事奏裁，小事立斷。

translations.literal: The Touring Inspector, however, represented the Son of Heaven on a tour of inspection; over enfeoffed ministers and prefectural, subprefectural, and county officials he conducted all reviews, with impeachment especially his charge; major matters he reported for imperial decision, minor matters he decided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The Touring Inspector represented the emperor on inspection tours; over enfeoffed princes and prefectural and county officials he conducted reviews and impeachments, reporting major cases to the throne and deciding minor ones on the spot.

sentences.zh: 按臨所至，必先審錄罪囚，吊刷案卷，有故出入者理辯之。

translations.literal: Wherever his inspection reached, he first reviewed and recorded criminal prisoners, examined and refreshed case files, and argued any who had been wrongly admitted or released.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he toured he first reviewed prisoners and case files, and argued any who had been wrongly convicted or released.

sentences.zh: 諸祭祀壇場，省其牆宇祭器。

translations.literal: At all sacrificial altars and sites he inspected their walls, buildings, and ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected sacrificial altars and their walls, buildings, and ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 存恤孤老，巡視倉庫，查算錢糧，勉勵學校，表揚善類，翦除豪蠹，以正風俗，振綱紀。

translations.literal: He succored orphans and the aged, inspected storehouses, audited money and grain, encouraged schools, commended the virtuous, cut down powerful parasites, to rectify customs and revive discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He succored orphans and the elderly, inspected storehouses, audited revenue, encouraged schools, commended the virtuous, and uprooted powerful parasites—to rectify local customs and restore discipline.

sentences.zh: 凡朝會糾儀，祭祀監禮。

translations.literal: At all court assemblies he corrected ceremonial order; at sacrifices he supervised ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies he corrected ceremonial order; at sacrifices he supervised ritual.

sentences.zh: 凡政事得失，軍民利病，皆得直言無避。

translations.literal: On all gains and losses in government and benefits and harms to troops and civilians, he might speak frankly without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: On policy successes and failures and the welfare of soldiers and civilians he could speak frankly without restraint.

sentences.zh: 有大政，集闕廷預議焉。

translations.literal: On great affairs of state he assembled at the palace gate court to deliberate in advance.
translations.idiomatic: On major state affairs he assembled at the palace gate court for preliminary deliberation.

sentences.zh: 蓋六部至重，然有專司，而都察院總憲綱，惟所見聞得糾察。

translations.literal: The Six Ministries were weightiest, yet each had its specialized charge; the Censorate held the overall disciplinary framework and might impeach whatever came within sight or hearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Ministries were weightiest, yet each had its specialty; the Censorate held overall disciplinary authority and could impeach whatever came to its attention.

sentences.zh: 諸御史糾劾，務明著實跡，開寫年月，毋虛文泛詆，訐拾細瑣。

translations.literal: In all impeachments by censors, they must clearly set forth verified facts, record year and month, and must not use empty rhetoric, broad slander, or pick up petty trifles.
translations.idiomatic: Censors' impeachments had to state verified facts with dates; empty rhetoric, broad slander, and petty grievances were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 出按復命，都御史覆劾其稱職不稱職以聞。

translations.literal: On return from touring inspection and reporting back, the Censor-in-Chief reviewed impeachment of whether they had performed their duties and reported accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When touring censors returned and reported, the Censor-in-Chief reviewed their performance and reported whether they had discharged their duties.

sentences.zh: 凡御史犯罪，加三等，有贓從重論。

translations.literal: Whenever a censor committed a crime, three degrees were added to the penalty; if there was corruption, punishment was increased.
translations.idiomatic: Censors who committed crimes faced penalties three degrees heavier; corruption drew still harsher punishment.

sentences.zh: 十三道各協管兩京、直隸衙門；

translations.literal: Each of the thirteen circuits jointly supervised offices in both capitals and Directly Administered prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Each of the thirteen circuits jointly supervised offices in both capitals and the directly administered prefectures;

sentences.zh: 而都察院衙門分屬河南道，獨專諸內外考察。

translations.literal: while the Censorate yamen itself was assigned to the Henan Circuit, which alone handled all internal and external performance reviews.
translations.idiomatic: the Censorate yamen itself fell under the Henan Circuit, which alone handled all internal and external performance reviews.

sentences.zh: 浙江道協管中軍都督府，在京府軍左、金吾左、金吾右、金吾前、留守中、神策、應天、和陽、廣洋、武功中、武功後、茂陵十二衛，牧馬千戶所，及直隸廬州府，廬州、六安二衛。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang Circuit jointly supervised the Central Military Commission, in the capital the twelve guards Fuyou Left, Jinyou Left, Jinyou Right, Jinyou Front, Rear Garrison Central, Shence, Yingtian, Heyang, Guangyang, Wugong Central, Wugong Rear, and Maoling, the Horse-Pasturing Battalion, and in the directly administered prefectures Luzhou Prefecture and the Luzhou and Lu'an guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang Circuit supervised the Central Military Commission, twelve capital guards (including Fuyou Left, the four Jinyou guards, Rear Garrison Central, Shence, Yingtian, Heyang, Guangyang, Wugong Central and Rear, and Maoling), the Horse-Pasturing Battalion, and in the provinces Luzhou Prefecture with the Luzhou and Lu'an guards.

sentences.zh: 江西道協管前軍都督府，在京府軍前、燕山左、龍江左、龍江右、龍驤、豹韜、天策、寬河八衛，及直隸淮安府，淮安、大河、邳州、九江、武清、龍門各衛。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi Circuit jointly supervised the Forward Military Commission, in the capital the eight guards Fuyou Front, Yanshan Left, Longjiang Left, Longjiang Right, Longxiang, Baotao, Tiance, and Kuanhe, and in the directly administered prefectures Huaian Prefecture and the Huaian, Dahe, Pizhou, Jiujiang, Wuqing, and Longmen guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi Circuit supervised the Forward Military Commission, eight capital guards (Fuyou Front, Yanshan Left, the two Longjiang guards, Longxiang, Baotao, Tiance, and Kuanhe), Huaian Prefecture, and the Huaian, Dahe, Pizhou, Jiujiang, Wuqing, and Longmen guards.

sentences.zh: 福建道協管戶部，寶鈔提舉司，鈔紙、印鈔二局，承運、廣惠、廣積、廣盈、贓罰、甲乙丙丁戊字、天財、軍儲、供用、行用各庫，在京金吾後、武成中、飛熊、武功左、武功右、武功前、獻陵、景陵、裕陵、泰陵十衛，及直隸常州、池州二府，定邊、開平中屯二衛，美峪千戶所。

translations.literal: The Fujian Circuit jointly supervised the Ministry of Revenue, the Paper Currency Directorate, the Paper and Printing Bureaus, the Chengyun, Guanghui, Guangji, Guangying, Forfeiture, Jia-Yi-Bing-Ding-Wu, Tiancai, Junchu, Gongyong, and Xingyong treasuries, in the capital the ten guards Jinyou Rear, Wucheng Central, Feixiong, Wugong Left, Wugong Right, Wugong Front, Xianling, Jingling, Yuling, and Tailing, and in the directly administered prefectures Changzhou and Chizhou prefectures, the Dingbian and Kaiping Central Garrison guards, and the Meiyu Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian Circuit supervised the Ministry of Revenue, the Paper Currency Directorate and its bureaus, numerous treasuries, ten capital guards (Jinyou Rear through Tailing), Changzhou and Chizhou prefectures, the Dingbian and Kaiping Central Garrison guards, and the Meiyu Battalion.

sentences.zh: 四川道協管工部，營繕所，文思院，御用、司設、神宮、尚衣、都知等監，惜薪司，兵仗、銀作、巾帽、針工、器皿、盔甲、軍器、寶源、皮作、鞍轡、織染、柴炭、抽分竹木各局，僧、道錄司，在京府軍、濟州、大寧前、蔚州左、永清左五衛，蕃牧千戶所，及直隸松江府、廣德州，金山、懷安、懷來各衛，神木千戶所，播州宣慰司，石砫、西陽等宣撫司，天全六番招討司。

translations.literal: The Sichuan Circuit jointly supervised the Ministry of Works, the Construction Office, the Literary Crafts Institute, the Imperial, Provision, Spirit Palace, Imperial Wardrobe, and Imperial Knowledge directorates and the like, the Fuelwood Office, the Arms, Silverwork, Headgear, Needlework, Vessels, Armor, Military Stores, Baoyuan, Leatherwork, Saddlery, Weaving and Dyeing, Charcoal, and Bamboo-Timber Apportionment bureaus, the Buddhist and Daoist Registries, in the capital the five guards Fuyou, Jizhou, Daning Front, Yuzhou Left, and Yongqing Left, the Fanmu Battalion, and in the directly administered prefectures Songjiang Prefecture and Guangde Prefecture, the Jinshan, Huaian, and Huailai guards, the Shenmu Battalion, the Bozhou Pacification Commission, the Shizhu and Xiyang Pacification Commissions, and the Tianquan Six Circuits Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan Circuit supervised the Ministry of Works and its workshops and directorates, numerous craft bureaus, the Buddhist and Daoist Registries, five capital guards, the Fanmu Battalion, Songjiang and Guangde prefectures, frontier guards and battalions, and the Bozhou, Shizhu, Xiyang, and Tianquan pacification offices.

sentences.zh: 陝西道協管後軍都督府，大理寺，行人司，在京府軍後、鷹揚、興武、義勇右、橫海、江陰、康陵、昭陵八衛，敢勇、報效二營，韓、秦、慶、安化四府，及直隸和州，保定左、右、中、前四衛。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Circuit jointly supervised the Rear Military Commission, the Court of Judicial Review, the Foreign Envoys Office, in the capital the eight guards Fuyou Rear, Yingyang, Xingwu, Yiyong Right, Henghai, Jiangyin, Kangling, and Zhaoling, the Ganyong and Baoxiao camps, the four princely establishments of Han, Qin, Qing, and Anhua, and in the directly administered prefectures He Prefecture and the Baoding Left, Right, Central, and Front guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi Circuit supervised the Rear Military Commission, the Court of Judicial Review, the Foreign Envoys Office, eight capital guards, the Ganyong and Baoxiao camps, the Han, Qin, Qing, and Anhua princely establishments, He Prefecture, and the four Baoding guards.

sentences.zh: 雲南道協管順天府，廣備庫，在京羽林前、通州二衛，及直隸永平、廣平二府，通州左、通州右、涿鹿、涿鹿左、涿鹿中、密雲中、密雲後、永平、山海、盧龍、撫寧、東勝左、東勝右、大同中屯、營州五屯、延慶、延慶左、延慶右、萬全左、萬全右各衛，居庸關、黃花鎮、寬河、武定各千戶所。

translations.literal: The Yunnan Circuit jointly supervised Shuntian Prefecture, the Broad Reserve Treasury, in the capital the two guards Yulin Front and Tongzhou, and in the directly administered prefectures Yongping and Guangping prefectures, the Tongzhou Left, Tongzhou Right, Zhuolu, Zhuolu Left, Zhuolu Central, Miyun Central, Miyun Rear, Yongping, Shanhai, Lulong, Funing, Dongsheng Left, Dongsheng Right, Datong Central Garrison, Yingzhou Five Garrisons, Yanqing, Yanqing Left, Yanqing Right, Wanquan Left, and Wanquan Right guards, and the Juyong Pass, Huanghua Town, Kuanhe, and Wuding battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan Circuit supervised Shuntian Prefecture, the Broad Reserve Treasury, the Yulin Front and Tongzhou guards in the capital, Yongping and Guangping prefectures, numerous northern garrison guards, and the Juyong Pass, Huanghua Town, Kuanhe, and Wuding battalions.

sentences.zh: 河南道協管禮部，都察院，翰林院，國子監，太常寺，光祿寺，鴻臚寺，尚寶司，中書舍人，欽天監，太醫院，司禮、尚膳、尚寶、直殿等監，酒醋面局，鐘鼓司，教坊司，在京羽林左、留守前、留守後、神武左、神武前、彭城六衛，伊、唐、周、鄭四府，及兩淮鹽運司，直隸揚州、大名二府，揚州、高郵、儀真、歸德、寧山、潼關、神武右各衛，泰州、通州、汝寧各千戶所。

translations.literal: The Henan Circuit jointly supervised the Ministry of Rites, the Censorate, the Hanlin Academy, the Directorate of Education, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Court of State Ceremonial, the Imperial Seals Office, Secretariat Drafters, the Astronomical Observatory, the Imperial Medical Institute, the Directorate of Ceremonies, Imperial Provisions, Imperial Seals, Palace Attendance, and the like, the Wine-Vinegar-Flour Office, the Bell and Drum Office, the Music Office, in the capital the six guards Yulin Left, Front Garrison, Rear Garrison, Shenwu Left, Shenwu Front, and Pengcheng, the four princely establishments of Yi, Tang, Zhou, and Zheng, the Liang-Huai Salt Transport Commission, and in the directly administered prefectures Yangzhou and Daming prefectures, the Yangzhou, Gaoyou, Yizhen, Guide, Ningshan, Tongguan, and Shenwu Right guards, and the Taizhou, Tongzhou, and Runing battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Circuit supervised the Ministry of Rites, the Censorate, the Hanlin Academy, the Directorate of Education, ritual and ceremonial courts, palace offices, six capital guards, the Yi, Tang, Zhou, and Zheng princely establishments, the Liang-Huai Salt Transport Commission, Yangzhou and Daming prefectures, and associated guards and battalions.

sentences.zh: 廣西道協管通政司，六科，在京燕山右、燕山前、大興左、騰驤左、騰驤右、武驤左、鎮南、瀋陽左、會州、富峪、忠義前、忠義後十二衛，及直隸安慶、徽州、保定、真定四府，安慶、新安、鎮武、真定各衛，紫荊關、倒馬關、廣昌各千戶所。

translations.literal: The Guangxi Circuit jointly supervised the Office of Transmission, the Six Offices of Scrutiny, in the capital the twelve guards Yanshan Right, Yanshan Front, Daxing Left, Tengxiang Left, Tengxiang Right, Wuxiang Left, Zhennan, Shenyang Left, Huizhou, Fuyu, Zhongyi Front, and Zhongyi Rear, and in the directly administered prefectures Anqing, Huizhou, Baoding, and Zhending prefectures, the Anqing, Xin'an, Zhenwu, and Zhending guards, and the Zijing Pass, Daoma Pass, and Guangchang battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi Circuit supervised the Office of Transmission, the Six Offices of Scrutiny, twelve capital guards, Anqing, Huizhou, Baoding, and Zhending prefectures, the Anqing, Xin'an, Zhenwu, and Zhending guards, and the Zijing, Daoma, and Guangchang pass battalions.

sentences.zh: 廣東道協管刑部，應天府，在京虎賁左、濟陽、武驤右、瀋陽右、武功左、武功右、孝陵、長陵八衛，及直隸延慶州，開平中屯衛。

translations.literal: The Guangdong Circuit jointly supervised the Ministry of Justice, Yingtian Prefecture, in the capital the eight guards Huben Left, Jiyang, Wuxiang Right, Shenyang Right, Wugong Left, Wugong Right, Xiaoling, and Changling, and in the directly administered prefectures Yanqing Subprefecture and the Kaiping Central Garrison guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong Circuit supervised the Ministry of Justice, Yingtian Prefecture, eight capital guards (Huben Left through Changling), Yanqing Subprefecture, and the Kaiping Central Garrison guard.

sentences.zh: 山西道協管左軍都督府，在京錦衣、府軍右、留守左、驍騎左、驍騎右、龍虎、龍虎左、大寧中、義勇前、義勇後、英武、水軍左十二衛，晉府長史司，及直隸鎮江、太平二府，鎮江、建陽、瀋陽中屯各衛，平定、蒲州二千戶所。

translations.literal: The Shanxi Circuit jointly supervised the Left Military Commission, in the capital the twelve guards Jinyi, Fuyou Right, Left Garrison, Xiaoqi Left, Xiaoqi Right, Longhu, Longhu Left, Daning Central, Yiyong Front, Yiyong Rear, Yingwu, and Shuijun Left, the Jin Establishment Chief Secretary's Office, and in the directly administered prefectures Zhenjiang and Taiping prefectures, the Zhenjiang, Jianyang, and Shenyang Central Garrison guards, and the Pingding and Puzhou battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanxi Circuit supervised the Left Military Commission, twelve capital guards, the Jin princely establishment, Zhenjiang and Taiping prefectures, the Zhenjiang, Jianyang, and Shenyang Central Garrison guards, and the Pingding and Puzhou battalions.

sentences.zh: 山東道協管宗人府，兵部，會同館，御馬監，典牧所，大通關，在京羽林右、永清右、濟川三衛，及中都留守司，遼東都司，直隸鳳陽府，徐、滁二州，中都留守左、留守中、鳳陽、鳳陽中、鳳陽右、皇陵、長淮、懷遠、徐州、滁州、泗州、壽州、宿州、武平、沂州、德州、德州左、保定後、瀋陽中各衛，洪塘千戶所。

translations.literal: The Shandong Circuit jointly supervised the Court of the Imperial Clan, the Ministry of War, the Hostel for Tributary Envoys, the Imperial Horse Directorate, the Herd Office, the Datong Pass, in the capital the three guards Yulin Right, Yongqing Right, and Jichuan, the Zhongdu Garrison Commission, the Liaodong Regional Command, in the directly administered prefectures Fengyang Prefecture and Xu and Chu prefectures, the Zhongdu Left Garrison, Central Garrison, Fengyang, Fengyang Central, Fengyang Right, Imperial Mausoleum, Changhuai, Huaiyuan, Xuzhou, Chuzhou, Sizhou, Shouzhou, Suzhou, Wuping, Yizhou, Dezhou, Dezhou Left, Baoding Rear, and Shenyang Central guards, and the Hongtang Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong Circuit supervised the Court of the Imperial Clan, the Ministry of War, the tributary hostel, the Imperial Horse Directorate, three capital guards, the Zhongdu and Liaodong commands, Fengyang Prefecture, Xu and Chu prefectures, numerous guards across the ancestral homeland, and the Hongtang Battalion.

sentences.zh: 湖廣道協管右軍都督府，五城兵馬司，在京留守右、武德、忠義右、虎賁右、廣武、水軍右、江淮、永陵八衛，遼、梁、岷、吉、華陽五府，荊、襄、楚三府長史司，及興都留守司，直隸甯國府，甯國、宣州、神武中、定州、茂山各衛。

translations.literal: The Huguang Circuit jointly supervised the Right Military Commission, the Five-Wards Military Patrol Office, in the capital the eight guards Right Garrison, Wude, Zhongyi Right, Huben Right, Guangwu, Shuijun Right, Jianghuai, and Yongling, the five princely establishments of Liao, Liang, Min, Ji, and Huayang, the chief secretary's offices of the Jing, Xiang, and Chu establishments, the Xingdu Garrison Commission, and in the directly administered prefectures Ningguo Prefecture and the Ningguo, Xuanzhou, Shenwu Central, Dingzhou, and Maoshan guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Huguang Circuit supervised the Right Military Commission, the Five-Wards Military Patrol Office, eight capital guards, the Liao, Liang, Min, Ji, and Huayang princely establishments, the Jing, Xiang, and Chu chief secretary's offices, the Xingdu Garrison Commission, Ningguo Prefecture, and the Ningguo, Xuanzhou, Shenwu Central, Dingzhou, and Maoshan guards.

sentences.zh: 貴州道協管吏部，太僕寺，上林苑監，內官、印綬二監，在京旗手衛，及長蘆鹽運司，大寧都司，萬全都司，直隸蘇州、河間、順德三府，保安州、蘇州、太倉、鎮海、薊州、遵化、鎮朔、興州五屯，忠義中、河間、天津、天津左、天津右、宣府前、宣府左、宣府右、開平、保安右、蔚州、永甯各衛，嘉興、吳淞江、梁城、滄州、興和、長安、龍門各千戶所。

translations.literal: The Guizhou Circuit jointly supervised the Ministry of Personnel, the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Imperial Park Directorate, the Inner Palace and Seals directorates, in the capital the Qishou guard, the Changlu Salt Transport Commission, the Daning and Wanquan regional commands, in the directly administered prefectures Suzhou, Hejian, and Shunde prefectures, Bao'an Subprefecture, and the Suzhou, Taicang, Zhenhai, Jizhou, Zunhua, Zhenshuo, and Xingzhou Five Garrisons, the Zhongyi Central, Hejian, Tianjin, Tianjin Left, Tianjin Right, Xuanfu Front, Xuanfu Left, Xuanfu Right, Kaiping, Bao'an Right, Yuzhou, and Yongning guards, and the Jiaxing, Wusong River, Liangcheng, Cangzhou, Xinghe, Chang'an, and Longmen battalions.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou Circuit supervised the Ministry of Personnel, the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Imperial Park Directorate, the Inner Palace and Seals directorates, the Qishou guard, the Changlu Salt Transport Commission, the Daning and Wanquan commands, Suzhou, Hejian, and Shunde prefectures, numerous northern garrison guards, and associated battalions.

sentences.zh: 初，吳元年置御史臺，設左、右御史大夫，從一品御史中丞，正二品侍御史，從二品治書侍御史，正三品殿中侍御史，正五品察院監察御史，正七品經歷，從五品都事，正七品照磨、管勾。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the first year of Wu the Censorate was established, with Left and Right Censor Grandees at rank 1b, Censor Vice Commissioners at rank 2a, Attending Censors at rank 2b, Secretariat Attending Censors at rank 3a, Palace Attending Censors at rank 5a, Investigation Office Investigating Censors at rank 7a, Registrars at rank 5b, Secretariat Clerks at rank 7a, and Copying Clerks and Controllers at rank 8a.
translations.idiomatic: Originally, in the first year of the Wu regime the Censorate was established with Left and Right Censor Grandees (rank 1b), Vice Commissioners (2a), Attending Censors (2b), Secretariat and Palace Attending Censors (3a and 5a), Investigating Censors (7a), and supporting staff down to rank 8a.

sentences.zh: 正八品以鄧愈、湯和為御史大夫，劉基、章溢為御史中丞，諭之曰：「國家立三大府，中書總政事，都督掌軍旅，御史掌糾察。

translations.literal: At rank 8a Deng Yu and Tang He were made Censor Grandees, Liu Ji and Zhang Yi Censor Vice Commissioners; they were instructed: "The state has established three great offices: the Secretariat oversees government affairs, the Military Commission commands armies, and the Censorate handles impeachment and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu and Tang He were appointed Censor Grandees and Liu Ji and Zhang Yi Vice Commissioners; they were told: "The state has three great offices: the Secretariat oversees government, the Military Commission commands armies, and the Censorate handles impeachment.

sentences.zh: 朝廷紀綱盡系於此，而臺察之任尤清要。

translations.literal: The court's discipline and framework all depend on this, and the charge of the Censorate is especially pure and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The court's discipline rested on all three, but the Censorate's charge was especially grave and honorable.

sentences.zh: 卿等當正己以率下，忠勤以事上，毋委靡因循以縱奸，毋假公濟私以害物。」

translations.literal: You must rectify yourselves to lead subordinates, serve the throne with loyalty and diligence, do not be lax and perfunctory thereby indulging wrongdoers, and do not use public office for private ends to harm others."
translations.idiomatic: Rectify yourselves to lead your subordinates, serve the throne loyally and diligently, do not grow lax and indulgent toward wrongdoing, and do not use public office for private gain."

sentences.zh: 洪武九年汰侍御史及治書、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu the Attending Censor and the Secretariat and Palace Attending Censor posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 9 the Attending Censor and the Secretariat and Palace Attending Censor posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，詔遣監察御史巡按州縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year an edict dispatched Investigating Censors to tour and inspect prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 10 an edict dispatched Investigating Censors to tour prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 十三年，專設左，右中丞，正二品左、右侍御史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Left and Right Vice Commissioners were established exclusively, and Left and Right Attending Censors at rank 2a.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 Left and Right Vice Commissioners were established, with Left and Right Attending Censors at rank 2a.

sentences.zh: 正四品尋罷御史臺。

translations.literal: At rank 4a; soon afterward the Censorate was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At rank 4a; soon afterward the Censorate itself was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十五年更置都察院，設監察都御史八人，秩正七品。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Censorate was re-established as the Censorate, with eight Investigating Censors-in-Chief at rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the Censorate was re-established with eight Investigating Censors-in-Chief at rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 分監察御史為浙江、河南、山東、北平、山西、陝西、湖廣、福建、江西、廣東、廣西、四川十二道，各道置御史或五人或三、四人，秩正九品。

translations.literal: Investigating Censors were divided into twelve circuits: Zhejiang, Henan, Shandong, Beiping, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huguang, Fujian, Jiangxi, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Sichuan; each circuit had five, or three or four censors, at rank 9a.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censors were divided into twelve circuits (Zhejiang through Sichuan); each circuit had three to five censors at rank 9a.

sentences.zh: 每道鑄印二，一畀御史久次者掌之，一藏內府，有事受印以出，既事納之，文曰：「繩愆糾繆」。

translations.literal: Each circuit cast two seals: one given to the censor of longest tenure to keep, one stored in the inner palace; when there was business the seal was received to go out, and when the matter was finished it was returned; the inscription read "Correct faults and rectify errors."
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit had two seals: one held by the senior censor, one stored in the inner palace; censors received a seal for business and returned it when finished. The inscription read "Correct faults and rectify errors."

sentences.zh: 以秀才李原名、詹徽等為都御史，吳荃等為試監察御史。

translations.literal: The scholar Li Yuanming, Zhan Hui, and others were made Censors-in-Chief; Wu Quan and others were made probationary Investigating Censors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanming, Zhan Hui, and other scholars were appointed Censors-in-Chief; Wu Quan and others were appointed probationary Investigating Censors.

sentences.zh: 試御史，一年後實授。

translations.literal: Probationary censors received full appointment after one year.
translations.idiomatic: Probationary censors received full appointment after one year.

sentences.zh: 又有理刑進士、理刑知縣，理都察院刑獄，半年實授。

translations.literal: There were also Judicial Administration jinshi and Judicial Administration magistrates who handled the Censorate's criminal cases; after half a year they received full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial Administration jinshi and magistrates also handled the Censorate's criminal cases, receiving full appointment after six months.

sentences.zh: 正德中革。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign these were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: These posts were abolished in the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 十六年，升都察院為正三品，設左、右都御史各一人，正三品，左、右副都御史各一人，正四品，左、右僉都御史各二人，正五品，經歷一人，正七品，知事一人，正八品。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Censorate was raised to rank 3a; one Left and one Right Censor-in-Chief were established at rank 3a, one Left and one Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at rank 4a, two Left and two Right Assistant Censors-in-Chief at rank 5a, one Registrar at rank 7a, and one Secretariat Clerk at rank 8a.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the Censorate was raised to rank 3a with one Left and one Right Censor-in-Chief (3a), one Vice Censor-in-Chief each side (4a), two Assistant Censors-in-Chief each side (5a), one Registrar (7a), and one Secretariat Clerk (8a).

sentences.zh: 十七年，升都御史正二品，副都御史正三品，僉都御史正四品，十二道監察御史正七品。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Censor-in-Chief was raised to rank 2a, the Vice Censor-in-Chief to rank 3a, the Assistant Censor-in-Chief to rank 4a, and the twelve-circuit Investigating Censors to rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the Censor-in-Chief rose to rank 2a, the Vice Censor-in-Chief to 3a, the Assistant Censor-in-Chief to 4a, and the twelve-circuit Investigating Censors to 7a.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，左副都御史袁泰言：「各道印篆相同，慮有詐偽。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai said: "The seal inscriptions of the various circuits are identical, and there is concern about fraud and forgery."
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai said: "The seal inscriptions of the various circuits are identical, raising concerns about fraud."

sentences.zh: 乃更鑄監察御史印曰：「某道監察御史印」，其巡按印曰：「巡按某處監察御史印」。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Investigating Censor seals were recast to read "Seal of the Investigating Censor of such-and-such Circuit," and the touring inspection seals to read "Seal of the Touring Investigating Censor of such-and-such Place."
translations.idiomatic: The Investigating Censor seals were recast as "Seal of the Investigating Censor of [circuit name]," and touring seals as "Seal of the Touring Investigating Censor of [place name]."

sentences.zh: 建文元年，改設都御史一人，革僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen one Censor-in-Chief was established and the Assistant Censor-in-Chief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen 1 a single Censor-in-Chief was established and the Assistant Censor-in-Chief abolished.

sentences.zh: 二年，改為御史府，設御史大夫，改十二道為左、右兩院，止設御史二十八人。

translations.literal: In the second year it was changed to the Censorate Bureau, with a Censor Grandee established; the twelve circuits were changed to Left and Right Bureaus, with only twenty-eight censors appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 it became the Censorate Bureau with a Censor Grandee; the twelve circuits became Left and Right Bureaus with only twenty-eight censors.

sentences.zh: 成祖復舊制。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor restored the former system.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzu Emperor restored the former system.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，改北平道為北京道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the Beiping Circuit was changed to the Beijing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 1 the Beiping Circuit became the Beijing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十八年，罷北京道，增設貴州、雲南、交阯三道。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Beijing Circuit was abolished and the Guizhou, Yunnan, and Jiaozhi circuits were added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 the Beijing Circuit was abolished and the Guizhou, Yunnan, and Jiaozhi circuits added.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，稱行在都察院，同六部，又定巡按以八月出巡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi it was styled the Traveling Censorate, on a par with the Six Ministries; it was also fixed that touring inspectors should set out in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi 1 it was styled the Traveling Censorate, equal to the Six Ministries; touring inspectors were fixed to depart in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年，罷交阯道，始定為十三道。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuande the Jiaozhi Circuit was abolished, and the thirteen circuits were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 10 the Jiaozhi Circuit was abolished and the thirteen circuits fixed.

sentences.zh: 正統中，去「行在。」

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong reign the words "Traveling"
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong reign the word "Traveling"

sentences.zh: 字。

translations.literal: were removed.
translations.idiomatic: was dropped from the title.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，以清屯，增副都御史三人，尋罷。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign, for garrison land review, three Vice Censors-in-Chief were added; soon they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiajing reign three Vice Censors-in-Chief were added for garrison land review, then soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，以提督京營，增右都御史三人，尋亦罷。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign, for supervision of the capital garrisons, three Right Censors-in-Chief were added; soon they too were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the Longqing reign three Right Censors-in-Chief were added to supervise the capital garrisons, then soon abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 總督宣大、山西等處軍務兼理糧餉一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of military affairs in Xuanhua-Datong, Shanxi, and other places, concurrently managing provisions and pay.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for military affairs in Xuanhua-Datong, Shanxi, and related regions, concurrently managing provisions and pay.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，始遣僉都御史巡撫宣大。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong an Assistant Censor-in-Chief was first dispatched as Grand Coordinator of Xuanhua-Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 an Assistant Censor-in-Chief was first dispatched as Grand Coordinator of Xuanhua-Datong.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，宣府、大同各設巡撫，遣尚書石璞總理軍務。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai Grand Coordinators were established separately for Xuanfu and Datong, and Minister Shi Pu was dispatched to oversee military affairs overall.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 2 separate Grand Coordinators were established for Xuanfu and Datong, and Minister Shi Pu was dispatched to oversee military affairs overall.

sentences.zh: 成化、弘治間，有警則遣。

translations.literal: Between the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, when there was an alarm one was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, one was dispatched when emergencies arose.

sentences.zh: 正德八年設總制。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengtong the post of Overall Commander was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 8 the post of Overall Commander was established.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，兼轄偏、保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, [the post] also had jurisdiction over Pian Pass and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign it also had jurisdiction over Pianguan and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，去偏、保，定設總督宣大、山西等處銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Pian and Baoding were removed, and the title Governor-General of Xuanhua-Datong, Shanxi, and other places was fixedly established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 Pianguan and Baoding were dropped from its jurisdiction, and the title Governor-General for Xuanhua-Datong, Shanxi, and related regions was permanently established.

sentences.zh: 三十八年令防秋日駐宣府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year it was ordered that during autumn defense [the incumbent] should be stationed at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 38 it was ordered to station at Xuanfu during the autumn defense season.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，移駐懷來。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, [the headquarters] was moved to Huailai.
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 the headquarters moved to Huailai.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，移駐陽和。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing, [the headquarters] was moved to Yanghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 4 it moved to Yanghe.

sentences.zh: 總督陝西三邊軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of military affairs for the Three Frontiers of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for military affairs on the Shaanxi Three Frontiers.

sentences.zh: 弘治十年，火篩入寇，議遣重臣總督陝西、甘肅、延綏、寧夏軍務，乃起左都御史王越任之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongzhi, Huosha invaded; it was proposed to dispatch a senior minister as Governor-General of military affairs in Shaanxi, Gansu, Yan'an-Suiyuan, and Ningxia, and so the Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue was recalled to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 10 Huosha raided the frontier; the court proposed dispatching a senior minister as Governor-General for military affairs in Shaanxi, Gansu, Yan'an-Suiyuan, and Ningxia, and recalled Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Yue to take the post.

sentences.zh: 十五年以後，或設或罷。

translations.literal: After the fifteenth year, [the post] was sometimes established and sometimes abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After year 15 the post was established or abolished as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖四年，始定設，初稱提督軍務。

translations.literal: Down to the fourth year of Jiajing it was first permanently established; at first it was called Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A permanent post was not fixed until Jiajing year 4; it was initially titled Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年改為總制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was changed to Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 the title was changed to Overall Commander.

sentences.zh: 十九年避制字，改為總督，開府固原，防秋駐花馬池。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, to avoid the character zhi [in the title], it was changed to Governor-General; [the office] opened headquarters at Guyuan, and during autumn defense [the incumbent] was stationed at Huamachi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19, to avoid the tabooed character in the title, it was renamed Governor-General; headquarters were opened at Guyuan, with autumn defense duty at Huamachi.

sentences.zh: 總督兩廣軍務兼理糧餉帶管鹽法兼巡撫廣東地方一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of military affairs for the Two Guang, concurrently managing provisions and pay, in charge of salt administration, and also Grand Coordinator of Guangdong—one post.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for Two Guang military affairs, concurrently managing provisions and pay, overseeing salt administration, and serving as Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，遣給事中雷填巡撫廣西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle a Supervising Secretary, Lei Tian, was dispatched as Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 Supervising Secretary Lei Tian was dispatched as Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遣郭瑄、艾廣巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Guo Xuan and Ai Guang were dispatched as Grand Coordinators of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 Guo Xuan and Ai Guang were dispatched as Grand Coordinators of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，苗寇起，以兩廣宜協濟應援，乃設總督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai Miao bandits rose; because the Two Guang should coordinate relief and mutual support, a Governor-General was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 3 Miao bandits rose; because the Two Guang needed coordinated relief and mutual support, a Governor-General was established.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，兼巡撫事，駐梧州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua [the post] also took on Grand Coordinator duties, stationed at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 it also assumed Grand Coordinator duties and was stationed at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 正德十四年，改總督為總制，尋改提督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong the Governor-General was changed to Overall Commander, and soon after to Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 14 the title was changed from Governor-General to Overall Commander, then soon to Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十五年，另設廣東巡撫，改提督為總督，止兼巡撫廣西，駐肇慶。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Jiajing a separate Guangdong Grand Coordinator was established; the Military Superintendent was changed back to Governor-General, with concurrent duty only as Grand Coordinator of Guangxi, stationed at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 45 a separate Guangdong Grand Coordinator was created; the Military Superintendent became Governor-General again, concurrently coordinating only Guangxi, stationed at Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，又設廣西巡撫，除兼職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing a Guangxi Grand Coordinator was again established, removing the concurrent duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 3 a Guangxi Grand Coordinator was established again, ending the concurrent arrangement.

sentences.zh: 四年，革廣東巡撫，改為提督兩廣軍務兼理糧餉，巡撫廣東。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Guangdong Grand Coordinator was abolished; [the post] was changed to Military Superintendent of Two Guang military affairs concurrently managing provisions and pay, and Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Guangdong Grand Coordinator was abolished; the title became Military Superintendent of Two Guang military affairs with concurrent management of provisions and pay, serving as Grand Coordinator of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，仍改總督，加帶管鹽法。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli it was again changed to Governor-General, with added charge of salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 3 it reverted to Governor-General, with added oversight of salt administration.

sentences.zh: 總督四川、陝西、河南、湖廣等處軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of military affairs in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Huguang, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for military affairs in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Henan, Huguang, and related regions.

sentences.zh: 正德五年設，尋罷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong it was established, and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Zhengtong year 5, it was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十七年，以苗患，又設總督四川、湖廣、貴州、雲南等處軍務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jiajing, because of Miao troubles, a Governor-General of military affairs in Sichuan, Huguang, Guizhou, Yunnan, and other places was again established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 27, owing to Miao unrest, a Governor-General for military affairs in Sichuan, Huguang, Guizhou, Yunnan, and related regions was re-established.

sentences.zh: 四十二年罷。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 42.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，以土官奢崇明反，又設四川、湖廣、雲南、貴州、廣西五省總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, because the native official She Chongming rebelled, a five-province Governor-General for Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi was again established.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, after the native official She Chongming rebelled, a Governor-General spanning Sichuan, Huguang, Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi was established again.

sentences.zh: 四年，兼巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year [the post] also served as Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 it also served as Grand Coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 總督浙江、福建、江南兼制江西軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General for Zhejiang, Fujian, and Jiangnan, concurrently controlling Jiangxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for Zhejiang, Fujian, and Jiangnan, concurrently directing Jiangxi military affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十三年，以倭犯杭州置。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Jiajing it was established because Japanese pirates attacked Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Jiajing year 33 after Wokou attacked Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四十一年革。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 41.

sentences.zh: 總督陝西、山西、河南、湖廣、四川五省軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of military affairs for the five provinces of Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for military affairs in Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan, Huguang, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年置，或兼七省。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen it was established, sometimes also covering seven provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 7, sometimes with jurisdiction over seven provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二年後，俱以內閣督師。

translations.literal: After the twelfth year, all [such duties] were assigned to Grand Secretaries supervising armies.
translations.idiomatic: After year 12 these duties were entrusted to Grand Secretaries serving as army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 總督鳳陽地方兼制河南、湖廣軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of Fengyang territory, concurrently controlling Henan and Huguang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for Fengyang territory, concurrently directing Henan and Huguang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年設。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 14.

sentences.zh: 總督保定地方軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General for Baoding territory military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for military affairs in Baoding territory.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年設。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 11.

sentences.zh: 總督河南、湖廣軍務兼巡撫河南一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General for Henan and Huguang military affairs, concurrently Grand Coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for Henan and Huguang military affairs, concurrently serving as Grand Coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年設。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 16.

sentences.zh: 總督九江地方兼制江西、湖廣軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Governor-General of Jiujiang territory, concurrently controlling Jiangxi and Huguang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Governor-General for Jiujiang territory, concurrently directing Jiangxi and Huguang military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年設。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 16.

sentences.zh: 總理南直隸、河南、山東、湖廣、四川軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Chief Coordinator of military affairs in Nanzhili, Henan, Shandong, Huguang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: One Chief Coordinator for military affairs in Nanzhili, Henan, Shandong, Huguang, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年設，以盧象昇為之，與總督或分或並。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen it was established, with Lu Xiangsheng appointed; [the post] was sometimes separate from and sometimes combined with the Governor-General.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 8 with Lu Xiangsheng appointed; its relationship to the Governor-General was sometimes divided and sometimes combined.

sentences.zh: 總理河漕兼提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Chief Coordinator of the Grand Canal and grain transport, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Chief Coordinator of the Grand Canal and grain transport, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年遣尚書治河，自後間遣侍郎、都御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle a Minister was dispatched to manage the Yellow River; thereafter Vice Ministers and Censors-in-Chief were occasionally dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 9 a Minister was sent to manage the Yellow River; thereafter Vice Ministers and Censors-in-Chief were dispatched from time to time.

sentences.zh: 成化後，始稱總督河道。

translations.literal: After Chenghua it was first called Governor-General of the river course.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chenghua reign it was first titled Governor-General of the river course.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，定設都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong a Censor-in-Chief was permanently established [for the post].
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 4 the post was permanently assigned to a Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十年，以都御史加工部職銜，提督河南、山東、直隸河道。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jiajing a Censor-in-Chief with added Ministry of Works rank supervised the river courses of Henan, Shandong, and Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 20 a Censor-in-Chief with added Ministry of Works rank supervised river works in Henan, Shandong, and Zhili.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，加提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing Military Superintendent of Affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 4 the title Military Superintendent of Affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年，改總理河漕兼提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli it was changed to Chief Coordinator of the Grand Canal and grain transport, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 5 it became Chief Coordinator of the Grand Canal and grain transport, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 八年革。

translations.literal: In the eighth year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 8.

sentences.zh: 總理糧儲提督軍務兼巡撫應天等府一員。

translations.literal: One Chief Coordinator of grain storage, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs and Grand Coordinator of Yingtian and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: One Chief Coordinator of grain storage, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs and Grand Coordinator of Yingtian and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，初命侍郎總督糧儲兼巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande a Vice Minister was first ordered as Governor-General of grain storage, concurrently Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 a Vice Minister was first appointed Governor-General of grain storage, concurrently serving as Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年，定遣都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingtai a Censor-in-Chief was fixedly dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 4 a Censor-in-Chief was permanently assigned to the post.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十三年，以海警，加提督軍務，駐蘇州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year of Jiajing, because of maritime alarms, Military Superintendent of Affairs was added, [with headquarters] stationed at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 33, owing to maritime alarms, Military Superintendent of Affairs was added, with headquarters at Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，移駐句容，已復駐蘇州。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign [headquarters] was moved to Jurong, then again stationed at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign headquarters moved to Jurong, then returned to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫浙江等處地方兼提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang and other places, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Zhejiang and related regions, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，遣尚書治兩浙農事。

translations.literal: In early Yongle a Minister was dispatched to manage agricultural affairs in the Two Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign a Minister was sent to oversee agricultural affairs in the Two Zhe.

sentences.zh: 以後或巡視或督鹺，有事則遣。

translations.literal: Thereafter [officials] were sometimes Inspectors or salt supervisors; when there was business one was dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter appointees served as Inspector or salt supervisor as needed; officials were dispatched when affairs arose.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年，以海警，始命都御史巡撫浙江，兼管福建福、興、建寧、漳、泉海道地方，提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing, because of maritime alarms, a Censor-in-Chief was first ordered as Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang, also managing the maritime circuits of Fujian Fu, Xing, Jianning, Zhang, and Quan, as Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 26, owing to maritime alarms, a Censor-in-Chief was first appointed Grand Coordinator of Zhejiang, also overseeing Fujian's Fu, Xing, Jianning, Zhang, and Quan maritime circuits, with the added title Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，改巡撫為巡視。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Grand Coordinator was changed to Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 the title Grand Coordinator was changed to Inspector.

sentences.zh: 二十八年罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 28.

sentences.zh: 三十一年復設。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established in year 31.

sentences.zh: 巡撫福建地方兼提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Fujian, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Fujian, concurrently Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年，既設浙江巡撫兼轄福、興、漳、泉等處，三十五年，以閩、浙道遠，又設提督軍務兼巡福、興、漳、泉、福寧海道都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing, after the Zhejiang Grand Coordinator was established with concurrent jurisdiction over Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and other places, in the thirty-fifth year, because the Fujian and Zhejiang routes were far apart, a Censor-in-Chief was again established as Military Superintendent of Affairs concurrently Grand Coordinator of the Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and Funing maritime circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 26 a Zhejiang Grand Coordinator was set up also governing Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and related districts; in year 35, because Fujian and Zhejiang were distant from each other, a Censor-in-Chief was added as Military Superintendent concurrently Grand Coordinator of the Fu, Xing, Zhang, Quan, and Funing maritime circuit.

sentences.zh: 後改巡撫福建，統轄全省。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to Grand Coordinator of Fujian, governing the entire province.
translations.idiomatic: Later the title became Grand Coordinator of Fujian, governing the whole province.

sentences.zh: 巡撫順天等府地方兼整飭薊州等處邊備一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Shuntian and other prefectures, concurrently reorganizing border defense at Jizhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Shuntian and related prefectures, concurrently reorganizing border defense at Jizhou and other posts.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，始專設都御史贊理軍務，巡撫順天、永平二府，尋兼撫河間、真定、保定，凡五府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua a Censor-in-Chief was first specially established to assist in military affairs, as Grand Coordinator of Shuntian and Yongping; soon it also coordinated Hejian, Zhending, and Baoding—five prefectures in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 2 a Censor-in-Chief was first dedicated to assisting in military affairs as Grand Coordinator of Shuntian and Yongping; soon Hejian, Zhending, and Baoding were added—five prefectures in all.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼理八府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year [the post] also managed eight prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 it also managed eight prefectures.

sentences.zh: 八年，以畿輔地廣，從居庸關中分，設二巡撫，其東為巡撫順天、永平二府，駐遵化。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because the metropolitan region was broad, from the center at Juyong Pass it was divided; two Grand Coordinators were established; the eastern one was Grand Coordinator of Shuntian and Yongping, stationed at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, because the metropolitan region was vast, the jurisdiction was split at Juyong Pass; two Grand Coordinators were created—the eastern one for Shuntian and Yongping, stationed at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，又於永平分設巡撫兼提督山海軍務，其舊者止轄順天。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen a separate Grand Coordinator was again established from Yongping, concurrently Military Superintendent of Shanhai military affairs; the original post governed only Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 2 a separate Yongping Grand Coordinator was added, concurrently Military Superintendent of Shanhai military affairs; the original post retained only Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 巡撫保定等府提督紫荊等關兼管河道一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Baoding and other prefectures, supervising Zijing and other passes, concurrently managing river works.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Baoding and related prefectures, supervising Zijing and other passes, concurrently managing river works.

sentences.zh: 成化八年，分居庸關以西，另設巡撫保定、真定、河間、順德、大名、廣平六府，提督紫荊、倒馬、龍泉等關，駐真定。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua, west of Juyong Pass a separate Grand Coordinator was established for the six prefectures of Baoding, Zhending, Hejian, Shunde, Daming, and Guangping, supervising Zijing, Daoma, Longquan, and other passes, stationed at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 8, west of Juyong Pass, a separate Grand Coordinator was set up for Baoding, Zhending, Hejian, Shunde, Daming, and Guangping, supervising Zijing, Daoma, Longquan, and other passes, stationed at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 萬曆七年，兼管河道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli [the post] also managed river works.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 7 it also took charge of river works.

sentences.zh: 巡撫河南等處地方兼管河道提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Henan and other places, concurrently managing river works and Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Henan and related regions, concurrently managing river works and serving as Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，遣兵部侍郎于謙巡撫山西、河南。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande Ministry of War Vice Minister Yu Qian was dispatched as Grand Coordinator of Shanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 Ministry of War Vice Minister Yu Qian was sent as Grand Coordinator of Shanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年，以左副都御史王來巡撫湖廣、河南。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Lai served as Grand Coordinator of Huguang and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 14 Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Lai served as Grand Coordinator of Huguang and Henan.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，始專設河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai a Henan Grand Coordinator was first specially established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 a dedicated Henan Grand Coordinator was first established.

sentences.zh: 萬曆七年，兼管河道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli [the post] also managed river works.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 7 it also took charge of river works.

sentences.zh: 八年，加提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Military Superintendent of Affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the title Military Superintendent of Affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 巡撫山西地方兼提督雁門等關軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Shanxi, concurrently Military Superintendent of military affairs at Yanmen and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Shanxi, concurrently Military Superintendent of affairs at Yanmen and other passes.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，以侍郎巡撫河南、山西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande a Vice Minister served as Grand Coordinator of Henan and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 a Vice Minister served as Grand Coordinator of Henan and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年，始命都御史專撫山西，鎮守雁門。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong a Censor-in-Chief was first ordered solely to coordinate Shanxi, garrisoning Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 13 a Censor-in-Chief was first assigned solely to coordinate Shanxi, garrisoning Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 天順、成化間暫革，尋復置。

translations.literal: Between the Tianshun and Chenghua reigns it was temporarily abolished, then soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was briefly abolished during the Tianshun and Chenghua reigns, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 巡撫山東等處地方督理營田兼管河道提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Shandong and other places, supervising garrison fields, concurrently managing river works and Military Superintendent of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Shandong and related regions, supervising garrison fields, concurrently managing river works and serving as Military Superintendent of Affairs.

sentences.zh: 正統五年始設巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong a Grand Coordinator was first established.
translations.idiomatic: A Grand Coordinator was first established in Zhengtong year 5.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定遣都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year a Censor-in-Chief was fixedly dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 a Censor-in-Chief was permanently assigned.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十二年，加督理營田。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Jiajing supervision of garrison fields was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 42 oversight of garrison fields was added.

sentences.zh: 萬曆七年，兼管河道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wanli [the post] also managed river works.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 7 it also took charge of river works.

sentences.zh: 八年，加提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Military Superintendent of Affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the title Military Superintendent of Affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 巡撫遼東地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Liaodong, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Liaodong, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 正統元年設，舊駐遼陽，後地日蹙，移駐廣寧，駐山海關，後又駐寧遠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong it was established; originally stationed at Liaoyang; later, as territory shrank daily, [headquarters] moved to Guangning, then Shanhai Pass, then again to Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Zhengtong 1, it was first stationed at Liaoyang; as territory steadily contracted, headquarters moved to Guangning, then Shanhai Pass, and finally Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 巡撫宣府地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Xuanfu, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，命都御史出巡塞北，因奏設巡撫兼理大同。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong a Censor-in-Chief was ordered to tour the northern frontier; on memorializing, a Grand Coordinator was established also managing Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 a Censor-in-Chief was sent to tour the northern frontier and, on memorializing, a Grand Coordinator was established also overseeing Datong.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，另設大同巡撫，後復並為一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingtai a separate Datong Grand Coordinator was established; later [the posts] were again merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 2 a separate Datong Grand Coordinator was created; later the two posts were merged again.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，復分設。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua [the posts] were again separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 10 they were split again.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year assisting in military affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the duty of assisting in military affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 巡撫大同地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Datong, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Datong, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 初與宣府共一巡撫，後或分或並。

translations.literal: At first [Xuanfu and Datong] shared one Grand Coordinator; later [the posts] were sometimes separate and sometimes combined.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Xuanfu and Datong shared one Grand Coordinator; later the arrangement alternated between separation and merger.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，復專設，加贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua [the post] was again exclusively established, with added duty of assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 10 it was re-established as a dedicated post, with added responsibility for assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 巡撫延綏等處贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Yan-sui and other places, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Yan-sui and related regions, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年，遣都御史出鎮。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuande a Censor-in-Chief was dispatched to garrison [the region].
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 10 a Censor-in-Chief was sent to take command in the field.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，專設巡撫加參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai a Grand Coordinator was exclusively established, with added participating supervision of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 a dedicated Grand Coordinator was established, with the added title of Participating Supervisor of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 成化九年，徙鎮榆林。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chenghua [headquarters] were moved to garrison at Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 9 the garrison was relocated to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，改贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing [the title] was changed to assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 6 the post was retitled to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 巡撫寧夏地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Ningxia, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Ningxia, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，以右僉都御史郭智鎮撫寧夏，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong the Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Guo Zhi was sent to pacify Ningxia and participate in supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1 the Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Guo Zhi was appointed to pacify Ningxia as Participating Supervisor of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天順元年罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun [the post] was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Tianshun 1.

sentences.zh: 二年復設，去參贊。

translations.literal: In the second year it was re-established, and the participating supervision [title] was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established in year 2, without the participating supervision title.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，加贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing assisting in military affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 6 the duty of assisting in military affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 巡撫甘肅等處贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Gansu and other places, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Gansu and related regions, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年，命侍郎鎮守。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuande a Vice Minister was ordered to garrison [the region].
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 10 a Vice Minister was appointed to garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 正統元年，甘、涼用兵，命侍郎參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong, because Gansu and Liangzhou were at war, a Vice Minister was ordered to participate in supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 1, with fighting in Gansu and Liangzhou, a Vice Minister was sent as Participating Supervisor of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，定設巡撫都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai a Grand Coordinator Censor-in-Chief was fixedly established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 the post of Grand Coordinator Censor-in-Chief was permanently established.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年，改贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Longqing [the title] was changed to assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 6 the post was retitled to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陝西地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Shaanxi, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，遣尚書、侍郎出鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande Ministers and Vice Ministers were dispatched to garrison [the region].
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xuande reign Ministers and Vice Ministers were sent to take field command.

sentences.zh: 正統間，命右都御史陳鎰、王文等出入更代。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi, Wang Wen, and others were ordered in rotation to replace one another.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong period the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Yi, Wang Wen, and others served in rotating succession.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，耿九疇以刑部侍郎出鎮，文移不得徑下按察司，特改都御史巡撫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai Geng Jiu-chou went out to garrison as Vice Minister of Justice; because documents could not be sent directly down to the Surveillance Commission, he was specially changed to Censor-in-Chief as Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai Geng Jiu-chou took field command as Vice Minister of Justice; because paperwork could not be routed directly to the provincial surveillance commission, he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief with the title Grand Coordinator.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，加提督軍務，後改贊理，駐西安，防秋駐固原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua Military Superintendent was added; later [the title] was changed to assisting [in military affairs]; [the office] was stationed at Xi'an, and for autumn defense at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 2 the title Military Superintendent was added; later it became assisting in military affairs, with headquarters at Xi'an and autumn defense at Guyuan.
