sentences.zh: 巡撫四川等處地方兼提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Sichuan and other places, concurrently Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Sichuan and related regions, concurrently serving as Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，命都御史鎮撫，後停遣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande a Censor-in-Chief was ordered to pacify [the region]; later dispatch was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 a Censor-in-Chief was appointed to pacify the region; later appointments ceased.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年，始設巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong a Grand Coordinator was first established.
translations.idiomatic: A Grand Coordinator was first established in Zhengtong year 14.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十一年，加提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli Military Superintendent was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 11 the title Military Superintendent was added.

sentences.zh: 巡撫湖廣等處地方兼贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Huguang and other places, concurrently assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Huguang and related regions, concurrently assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，命都御史賈諒鎮守，以後或侍郎或大理卿出撫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong the Censor-in-Chief Jia Liang was ordered to garrison; thereafter sometimes a Vice Minister or the Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review went out as Grand Coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 3 Censor-in-Chief Jia Liang was sent to garrison the region; thereafter the post was filled alternately by a Vice Minister or the chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年定設巡撫都御史兼贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai a Grand Coordinator Censor-in-Chief concurrently assisting in military affairs was fixedly established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 the post of Grand Coordinator Censor-in-Chief assisting in military affairs was permanently established.

sentences.zh: 萬曆八年，改為提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wanli [the title] was changed to Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 8 the post became Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 十二年，仍為贊理。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year [the title] again became assisting [in military affairs].
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 it reverted to assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 巡撫江西地方兼理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi, concurrently managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Jiangxi, also responsible for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 永樂後，間設巡撫鎮守。

translations.literal: After Yongle a Grand Coordinator was occasionally established to garrison [the province].
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle reign a Grand Coordinator was sometimes appointed to garrison Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 成化以後，定為巡撫，或有時罷遣。

translations.literal: After Chenghua [the post] was fixed as Grand Coordinator, though at times it was abolished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Chenghua reign onward the post was standardized as Grand Coordinator, though it was occasionally abolished.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年始定設。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing it was first fixedly established.
translations.idiomatic: Permanently established in Jiajing year 6.

sentences.zh: 四十年加兼理軍務。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year concurrent management of military affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 responsibility for military affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 巡撫南贛汀韶等處地方提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Nan-Gan, Ting, and Shao and other places, Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for southern Ganzhou, Tingzhou, Shaozhou, and related regions, serving as Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 弘治十年，始設巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongzhi a Grand Coordinator was first established.
translations.idiomatic: A Grand Coordinator was first appointed in Hongzhi year 10.

sentences.zh: 正德十一年，改提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhengde [the title] was changed to Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 11 the post became Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十五年，定巡撫銜，所轄南安、贛州、南雄、韶州、汀州並郴州地方，駐贛州。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Jiajing the Grand Coordinator title was fixed; jurisdiction covered Nan'an, Ganzhou, Nanxiong, Shaozhou, Tingzhou, and Chenzhou, with headquarters at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 45 the Grand Coordinator title was standardized over Nan'an, Ganzhou, Nanxiong, Shaozhou, Tingzhou, and Chenzhou, stationed at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫廣東地方兼贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Guangdong, concurrently assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Guangdong, concurrently assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，設巡撫，後以總督兼巡撫事，遂罷不設。

translations.literal: During Yongle a Grand Coordinator was established; later the Governor-General also handled Grand Coordinator duties, and [the separate post] was abolished and not re-established.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign a Grand Coordinator was appointed; later the Governor-General assumed those duties and the separate post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十五年，復另設巡撫，加贊理軍務。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Jiajing a separate Grand Coordinator was again established, with added assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 45 a separate Grand Coordinator was re-established, with added responsibility for assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年又罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished again in Longqing year 4.

sentences.zh: 巡撫廣西地方一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 廣西舊有巡撫，沿革不常。

translations.literal: Guangxi formerly had a Grand Coordinator, but the evolution [of the post] was irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi had long had a Grand Coordinator, but the post's history was irregular.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年復專設。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing it was again exclusively established.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established as a dedicated post in Longqing year 3.

sentences.zh: 巡撫雲南兼建昌、畢節等處地方贊理軍務兼督川、貴糧餉一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Yunnan concurrently coordinating Jianchang, Bijie, and other places, assisting in military affairs and supervising Sichuan and Guizhou grain pay—one post.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Yunnan, Jianchang, Bijie, and related regions, assisting in military affairs and supervising grain supplies for Sichuan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 正統九年，命侍郎參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengtong a Vice Minister was ordered to participate in supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 9 a Vice Minister was appointed as Participating Supervisor of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，設鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year a pacification garrison was established.
translations.idiomatic: A pacification command was established in year 10.

sentences.zh: 天順元年罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun [the post] was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Tianshun 1.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年復設。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established in Chenghua year 12.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十年，加兼理軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Jiajing concurrent management of military affairs was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 30 responsibility for military affairs was added.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，改贊理。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year [the title] was changed to assisting [in military affairs].
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 the title became assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，兼撫建昌、畢節等處。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing [the post] also coordinated Jianchang, Bijie, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 2 Jianchang, Bijie, and related regions were added to its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 巡撫貴州兼督理湖北、川東等處地方提督軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Guizhou, concurrently supervising Hubei, eastern Sichuan, and other places as Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Guizhou, concurrently supervising Hubei, eastern Sichuan, and related regions as Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 正統十四年，以苗亂置總督，鎮守貴州、湖北、川東等處。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhengtong, because of Miao unrest, a Governor-General was established to garrison Guizhou, Hubei, eastern Sichuan, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 14 a Governor-General was appointed to garrison Guizhou, Hubei, eastern Sichuan, and related regions owing to Miao rebellion.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，另設貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai a separate Guizhou Grand Coordinator was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 a separate Grand Coordinator for Guizhou was established.

sentences.zh: 成化八年罷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua [the post] was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Chenghua year 8.

sentences.zh: 十一年復設。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established in year 11.

sentences.zh: 正德二年又罷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished again in Zhengde year 2.

sentences.zh: 五年又復設。

translations.literal: In the fifth year it was again re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established again in year 5.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十二年，裁革總督，令巡撫兼理湖北、川東等處提督軍務。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Jiajing the Governor-General was abolished, and the Grand Coordinator was ordered concurrently to manage Hubei, eastern Sichuan, and other places as Military Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 42 the Governor-General was abolished and the Grand Coordinator was charged with military affairs in Hubei, eastern Sichuan, and related regions as Military Superintendent.

sentences.zh: 巡撫天津地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Tianjin, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Tianjin, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十五年，以倭陷朝鮮暫設，尋為定制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Wanli it was temporarily established because Japanese pirates overran Korea; soon it became a fixed institution.
translations.idiomatic: Established temporarily in Wanli year 25 after Wokou overran Korea; it soon became a permanent post.

sentences.zh: 巡撫登萊地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Dengzhou and Laizhou, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Dengzhou and Laizhou, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年設。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Tianqi 1.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年罷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Chongzhen year 2.

sentences.zh: 三年復設。

translations.literal: In the third year it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established in year 3.

sentences.zh: 巡撫安廬地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Anqing and Luzhou, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Anqing and Luzhou, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年設，以史可法為之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen it was established, with Shi Kefa appointed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 10, with Shi Kefa as the first appointee.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又增設安、太、池、廬四府巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Grand Coordinators for the four prefectures of Anqing, Taiping, Chizhou, and Luzhou were additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 separate Grand Coordinators were added for the prefectures of Anqing, Taiping, Chizhou, and Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫偏沅地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Pian-Yuan, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Pian-Yuan, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十七年，以徵播暫設，尋罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Wanli it was temporarily established for the campaign against Bozhou; soon it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Temporarily established in Wanli year 27 for the Bozhou campaign, it was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年後，或置或罷。

translations.literal: After the second year of Tianqi [the post] was sometimes established and sometimes abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianqi year 2 the post was intermittently established and abolished.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年定設。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen it was fixedly established.
translations.idiomatic: Permanently established in Chongzhen year 2.

sentences.zh: 巡撫密雲地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Miyun, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Miyun, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年設。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 11.

sentences.zh: 巡撫淮揚地方贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Huaiyang, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Huaiyang, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年設。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 11.

sentences.zh: 巡撫承天贊理軍務一員。

translations.literal: One Grand Coordinator of Chengtian, assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Coordinator for Chengtian, assisting in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年設。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Chongzhen year 16.

sentences.zh: 撫治鄖陽等處地方兼提督軍務一員，成化十二年，以鄖、襄流民屢叛，遣都御史安撫，因奏設官撫治之。

translations.literal: One Pacification Administrator of Yunyang and other places, concurrently Military Superintendent; in the twelfth year of Chenghua, because displaced people in Yun and Xiang repeatedly rebelled, a Censor-in-Chief was dispatched to pacify them, and on memorializing an official was established to administer pacification.
translations.idiomatic: One Pacification Administrator for Yunyang and related regions, concurrently Military Superintendent; in Chenghua year 12, after repeated rebellions by displaced people in the Yun and Xiang region, a Censor-in-Chief was sent to pacify them and, on memorializing, a dedicated pacification office was created.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年以撫治事權不專，添提督軍務兼撫治職銜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, because pacification authority was not exclusive, the added title Military Superintendent concurrently Pacification Administrator was instituted.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 2, because pacification authority was insufficiently concentrated, the combined title Military Superintendent and Pacification Administrator was added.

sentences.zh: 九年裁革，十一年復設。

translations.literal: In the ninth year it was abolished; in the eleventh year it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in year 9 and re-established in year 11.

sentences.zh: 贊理松潘地方軍務一員。

translations.literal: One [official] assisting in military affairs in Songpan—one post.
translations.idiomatic: One official assisting in military affairs at Songpan.

sentences.zh: 正統四年，以王翱為之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong Wang Ao was appointed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao was appointed in Zhengtong year 4.

sentences.zh: 通政司

translations.literal: Office of Transmission
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Transmission

sentences.zh: 通政使司。

translations.literal: Office of the Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of the Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 通政使一人，正三品；

translations.literal: One Commissioner of Transmission, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: One Commissioner of Transmission, rank 3a;

sentences.zh: 左、右通政各一人，謄黃右通政一人，正四品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Commissioners of Transmission one each, one Right Commissioner of Transmission for Imperial Yellow Transcripts, rank 4a;
translations.idiomatic: One Left and one Right Commissioner of Transmission, plus one Right Commissioner for imperial yellow transcripts, all rank 4a;

sentences.zh: 左、右參議各一人，正五品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Secretariat Councillors one each, rank 5a.
translations.idiomatic: One Left and one Right Secretariat Councillor, rank 5a.

sentences.zh: 其屬，經歷司，經歷一人，正七品；

translations.literal: Subordinates: a Registry, one Registrar, rank 7a;
translations.idiomatic: Under it was a registry with one registrar, rank 7a;

sentences.zh: 知事一人，正八品。

translations.literal: one Secretariat Clerk, rank 8a.
translations.idiomatic: and one secretariat clerk, rank 8a.

sentences.zh: 通政使，掌受內外章疏敷奏封駁之事。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Transmission was charged with receiving memorials and reports from within and without, presenting them [to the throne], sealing and forwarding them, and returning them with imperial rescripts.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of Transmission received all memorials and reports from inside and outside the court, presented them to the throne, forwarded sealed documents, and handled imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 凡四方陳情建言，申訴冤滯，或告不法等事，於底簿內謄寫訴告緣由，齎狀奏聞。

translations.literal: For all petitions and proposals from the four directions, appeals of lingering injustice, or reports of unlawful conduct and the like, the grounds of the complaint were copied in the base register and the petition was carried forward to be memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions, proposals, appeals of injustice, and reports of wrongdoing from across the realm were copied into the office register with the grounds of complaint, then forwarded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 凡天下臣民實封入遞，即於公廳啟視，節寫副本，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: Whenever subjects throughout the realm submitted sealed memorials by relay, they were opened and inspected in the public hall, abridged copies were made, and then they were memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Sealed memorials from subjects throughout the realm were opened in the public hall, copied in abridged form, and then presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 即五軍、六部、都察院等衙門，有事關機密重大者，其入奏仍用本司印信。

translations.literal: Even for the Five Military Commissions, Six Ministries, Censorate, and other offices, when matters concerned great confidentiality and weight, their memorials to the throne still used this office's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Five Military Commissions, Six Ministries, Censorate, and other agencies used this office's seal when presenting matters of great confidentiality and importance.

sentences.zh: 凡諸司公文、勘合辨驗允當，編號注寫，公文用「日照之記」、勘合用「驗正之記。」

translations.literal: For all offices' documents and travel credentials, once verification showed them proper, numbers were assigned and annotations made; documents used the stamp "Record of the Sun's Shining," and credentials used "Record of Verification and Correction."
translations.idiomatic: After verifying documents and travel credentials from all agencies, the office numbered and annotated them; documents received the stamp "Record of the Sun's Shining," and credentials "Record of Verification and Correction."

sentences.zh: 關防之。

translations.literal: [They were] stamped with official seals.
translations.idiomatic: Both were stamped with official seals.

sentences.zh: 凡在外之題本、奏本，在京之奏本，並受之，於早朝匯而進之。

translations.literal: All routine memorials and formal memorials from outside [the capital], and formal memorials from within [the capital], were alike received and, at the morning audience, gathered and forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: Routine and formal memorials from the provinces and formal memorials from the capital were all received and presented together at the morning audience.

sentences.zh: 有逕自封進者則參駁。

translations.literal: Those who on their own directly sealed and forwarded [memorials] were jointly impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who forwarded sealed memorials without going through the office was reported for impeachment.

sentences.zh: 午朝則引奏臣民之言事者，有機密則不時入奏。

translations.literal: At the noon audience they presented and memorialized subjects and commoners who had matters to report; when there was secrecy they entered and memorialized at no fixed time.
translations.idiomatic: At the noon audience the office presented petitioners from among officials and commoners; confidential matters were brought to the throne at any hour.

sentences.zh: 有違誤則籍而匯請。

translations.literal: When there were violations or errors they were registered and gathered for request [to the throne].
translations.idiomatic: Errors and irregularities were logged and submitted together for imperial review.

sentences.zh: 凡抄發、照駁諸司公移及勘合、訟牒、勾提件數、給繇人員，月終類奏，歲終通奏。

translations.literal: For all copied dispatches, returned office documents of the various offices, travel credentials, lawsuit papers, numbers of items summoned for investigation, and personnel granted leave permits, at month's end they were classified and memorialized, at year's end reported together.
translations.idiomatic: Copies issued, documents returned for correction, travel credentials, lawsuits, summons counts, and leave permits were tallied monthly and reported in full at year's end.

sentences.zh: 凡議大政、大獄及會推文武大臣，必參預。

translations.literal: For all deliberation on great policy, great trials, and joint recommendation of civil and military grandees, [the commissioner] must participate beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner had to take part in deliberations on major policy, major trials, and joint recommendations of high officials.

sentences.zh: 初，洪武三年置察言司，設司令二人，掌受四方章奏，尋罷。

translations.literal: At first, in the third year of Hongwu the Office for Scrutinizing Petitions was established, two Directors were appointed, charged with receiving memorials from the four directions, and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 the Office for Scrutinizing Petitions was established with two directors to receive memorials from across the realm, but it was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 十年置通政使司，以曾秉正為通政使，劉仁為左通政，諭之曰：「政猶水也，欲其常通，故以『通政』名官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Office of the Commissioner of Transmission was established; Zeng Bingzheng was made Commissioner of Transmission and Liu Ren Left Commissioner, and they were instructed, saying: "Government is like water—one wishes it always to flow; therefore the office is named 'Transmission of Government.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 the Office of the Commissioner of Transmission was created, with Zeng Bingzheng as commissioner and Liu Ren as left commissioner. The emperor told them: "Government is like water—it must keep flowing; that is why your office is called Transmission of Government.

sentences.zh: 卿其審命令以正百司，達幽隱以通庶務。

translations.literal: You should examine commands to rectify the hundred offices, reach what is hidden and obscure to connect the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Scrutinize imperial commands to keep every office in order, and bring hidden grievances to light so that all affairs may flow freely.

sentences.zh: 當執奏者勿忌避，當駁正者勿阿隨，當敷陳者毋隱蔽，當引見者毋留難。」

translations.literal: What ought to be presented—do not shun through fear; what ought to be corrected—do not curry favor; what ought to be set forth—do not conceal; what ought to be introduced—do not obstruct with difficulties.'
translations.idiomatic: Present what should be heard without fear; correct what should be reversed without flattery; set forth what should be known without concealment; introduce petitioners without obstruction.

sentences.zh: 十二年，撥承敕監給事中、殿廷儀禮司、九關通事使隸焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, supervising secretaries of the Seal-Receiving Directorate, the Hall Ceremonial Office, and the Nine Gates Transmission Envoys were transferred to its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 supervising secretaries from the Seal-Receiving Directorate, the Hall Ceremonial Office, and the nine-gates transmission envoys were placed under its authority.

sentences.zh: 建文中，改司為寺，通政使為通政卿，通政參議為少卿，寺丞增置左、右補闕，左、右拾遺各一人。

translations.literal: Under the Jianwen reign, the office was changed to a directorate, the Commissioner to Transmission Director, the Secretariat Councillor to Vice Director, and to the directorate assistants were added Left and Right Remonstrance Supplements and Left and Right Memorial Pickers one each.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jianwen the office became a directorate: the commissioner became transmission director, the councillor vice director, and left and right remonstrance supplements and memorial pickers were added to the staff.

sentences.zh: 成祖復舊制。

translations.literal: Chengzu restored the former system.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor restored the original organization.

sentences.zh: 成化二年，置提督謄黃右通政，不理司事，錄武官黃衛所襲替之故，以徵贊事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua a Right Commissioner of Transmission supervising imperial yellow transcripts was established, not administering office affairs, recording the grounds for succession and replacement in yellow registers of military guards and battalions, to support approval matters.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 2 a right commissioner was appointed solely to supervise imperial yellow transcripts for military succession registers, without handling routine transmission business.

sentences.zh: 萬曆九年革。

translations.literal: Abolished in the ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: The post was abolished in Wanli year 9.

sentences.zh: 大理寺

translations.literal: Court of Judicial Review
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review

sentences.zh: 大理寺。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 卿一人，正三品；

translations.literal: One Director, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: One director, rank 3a;

sentences.zh: 左、右少卿各一人，正四品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Vice Directors one each, rank 4a;
translations.idiomatic: One left and one right vice director, rank 4a;

sentences.zh: 左、右寺丞各一人，正五品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Directorate Assistants one each, rank 5a.
translations.idiomatic: One left and one right directorate assistant, rank 5a.

sentences.zh: 其屬，司務廳，司務二人，從九品；

translations.literal: Subordinates: an Office of Secretariat Affairs, two Secretariat Clerks, rank 9b;
translations.idiomatic: Under it was an office of secretariat affairs with two secretariat clerks, rank 9b;

sentences.zh: 左、右二寺，各寺正一人，正六品；

translations.literal: Left and Right Sections, each with one Section Director, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: left and right sections, each with one section director, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 寺副二人，從六品，後革右寺副一人；

translations.literal: two Section Vice Directors, rank 6b, later one Right Section Vice Director was abolished;
translations.idiomatic: two section vice directors, rank 6b, later reduced by one on the right;

sentences.zh: 評事四人，正七品，初設右評事八人，後革四人。

translations.literal: four Reviewing Officers, rank 7a; at first eight Right Reviewing Officers were established, later four were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: four reviewing officers, rank 7a; initially eight served on the right, later cut to four.

sentences.zh: 卿，掌審讞平反刑獄之政令。

translations.literal: The Director was charged with reviewing verdicts and rectifying the directives governing penal imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: The director reviewed verdicts and oversaw the rectification of penal judgments.

sentences.zh: 少卿、寺丞贊之。

translations.literal: Vice directors and directorate assistants assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors and directorate assistants assisted him.

sentences.zh: 左、右寺分理京畿、十三布政司刑名之事。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Sections respectively handled criminal cases of the capital region and the thirteen provincial administrations.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right sections divided criminal cases between the capital region and the thirteen provinces.

sentences.zh: 凡刑部、都察院、五軍斷事官所推問獄訟，皆移案牘，引囚徒，詣寺詳讞。

translations.literal: All inquests and lawsuits pushed by the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, and Five Military Commissions' judging officials were transferred with case documents, prisoners led, and brought to the court for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: Cases tried by the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, and Five Military Commissions were sent with dossiers and prisoners to the court for detailed review.

sentences.zh: 左、右寺寺正，各隨其所轄而覆審之。

translations.literal: The Section Directors of the Left and Right Sections each, according to their jurisdiction, conducted re-review.
translations.idiomatic: Each section director re-examined cases within his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 既按律例，必復問其款狀，情允罪服，始呈堂準擬具奏。

translations.literal: Having applied the code articles, they had to question again the particulars of the indictment; when the facts were fitting and the offense admitted, only then was it presented in court, approved for drafting, and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: After applying the statutes they re-examined the indictment; only when facts and guilt aligned was the verdict drafted and memorialized.

sentences.zh: 不則駁令改擬，曰照駁。

translations.literal: Otherwise they rejected and ordered revision of the draft, called zhao-bo [returned for correction].
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the draft was returned for correction—called zhao-bo.

sentences.zh: 三擬不當，則糾問官，曰參駁。

translations.literal: If three drafts were improper, then the responsible official was impeached and questioned, called can-bo [joint referral for censure].
translations.idiomatic: If three drafts still failed, the responsible official was censured—called can-bo.

sentences.zh: 有牾律失入者，調他司再訊，曰番異。

translations.literal: When there was contradiction of statutes or error in sentencing, [the case] was transferred to another office for re-inquest, called fan-yi [variance].
translations.idiomatic: Contradictions of statute or sentencing errors were sent to another office for re-trial—called fan-yi.

sentences.zh: 猶不愜，則請下九卿會訊，曰圓審。

translations.literal: If still unsatisfactory, then a request was made to send it down for joint inquest by the Nine Ministers, called yuan-shen [rounded review].
translations.idiomatic: If still unresolved, the case went to a joint inquest by the Nine Ministers—called yuan-shen.

sentences.zh: 已評允而招由未明，移再訊，曰追駁。

translations.literal: When already approved in review but the confession record was unclear, it was transferred for re-inquest, called zhui-bo [pursued rejection].
translations.idiomatic: If approved but the confession remained unclear, the case was sent back for further inquiry—called zhui-bo.

sentences.zh: 屢駁不合，則請旨發落，曰制決。

translations.literal: When repeatedly rejected without agreement, then an imperial order was requested for disposition, called zhi-jue [imperial decision].
translations.idiomatic: After repeated rejections without agreement, imperial disposition was sought—called zhi-jue.

sentences.zh: 凡獄既具，未經本寺評允，諸司毋得發遣。

translations.literal: For all cases already complete, before approval in review by this court the various offices might not dispatch [prisoners].
translations.idiomatic: No office might dispatch a prisoner until the court had approved the completed case.

sentences.zh: 誤則糾之。

translations.literal: If in error, then they were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Violations were impeached.

sentences.zh: 初，吳元年置大理司卿，秩正三品。

translations.literal: At first, in the Wu reign year the Director of the Judicial Review Office was established, rank 3a.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wu reign year a director of judicial review was appointed at rank 3a.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年革。

translations.literal: Abolished in the first year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Hongwu 1.

sentences.zh: 三年，置磨勘司，凡諸司刑名、錢糧，有冤濫隱匿者，稽其功過以聞。

translations.literal: In the third year the Verification Office was established; for criminal cases and grain funds of all offices, when there was injustice, excess, or concealment, their merits and faults were examined and reported.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 a verification office was set up to audit all offices' criminal and fiscal records for injustice or concealment and report officials' merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 尋亦革。

translations.literal: Soon it too was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年置磨勘司，設司令、司丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu the Verification Office was established, with a Director and Directorate Assistants appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 the verification office was re-established with a director and assistants.

sentences.zh: 七年增設司令一人，司丞五人，首領官五人，分為四科。

translations.literal: In the seventh year one more Director was added, five Directorate Assistants, five chief officials, divided into four sections.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 one more director, five assistants, and five section chiefs were added, organized into four sections.

sentences.zh: 十年革。

translations.literal: Abolished in the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in year 10.

sentences.zh: 十四年復置磨勘司，設司令一人，左、右司丞各一人，左、右司副各一人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Verification Office was restored, with one Director, Left and Right Directorate Assistants one each, Left and Right Directorate Vice Assistants one each.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the verification office was restored with one director, one left and one right assistant, and one left and one right vice assistant.

sentences.zh: 二十年復罷。

translations.literal: Abolished again in the twentieth year.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished again in year 20.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復置大理寺，改卿秩正五品，左、右少卿從五品，左、右寺丞正六品。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Court of Judicial Review was restored; the Director's rank was changed to 5a, Left and Right Vice Directors 5b, Left and Right Directorate Assistants 6a.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the court was restored: the director at rank 5a, vice directors at 5b, and directorate assistants at 6a.

sentences.zh: 其屬，左、右寺正各一人，寺副各二人，左評事四人，右評事八人。

translations.literal: Subordinates: Left and Right Section Directors one each, Section Vice Directors two each, four Left Reviewing Officers, eight Right Reviewing Officers.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff comprised one left and one right section director, two vice directors per section, four left reviewing officers, and eight on the right.

sentences.zh: 又置審刑司，共平庶獄。

translations.literal: The Office of Reviewing Punishments was also established, jointly settling ordinary cases.
translations.idiomatic: An Office of Reviewing Punishments was also set up to settle ordinary cases jointly.

sentences.zh: 凡大理寺所理之刑，審刑司復詳議之。

translations.literal: For all punishments handled by the Court of Judicial Review, the Office of Reviewing Punishments again deliberated in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Every sentence from the Court of Judicial Review was reviewed again in detail by the Office of Reviewing Punishments.

sentences.zh: 審刑司設左、右審刑各一人，正六品；

translations.literal: The Office of Reviewing Punishments had Left and Right Reviewers of Punishment one each, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: The office had one left and one right reviewer of punishment, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 左、右詳議各三人，正七品。

translations.literal: Left and Right Detailed Deliberators three each, rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: and three left and three right detailed deliberators, rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改建刑部、都察院、大理寺、審刑司、五軍斷事官署於太平門外，名其所曰貫城。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, Court of Judicial Review, Office of Reviewing Punishments, and Five Military Commissions' judging offices were rebuilt outside Taiping Gate, and the place was named Guancheng [Threaded City].
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the Ministry of Justice, Censorate, Court of Judicial Review, Office of Reviewing Punishments, and Five Military judging offices were moved outside Taiping Gate to a compound called Threaded City.

sentences.zh: 十九年罷審刑司。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Office of Reviewing Punishments was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Reviewing Punishments was abolished in year 19.

sentences.zh: 二十二年復，卿秩正三品。

translations.literal: Restored in the twenty-second year; the Director's rank was 3a.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in year 22, with the director again at rank 3a.

sentences.zh: 少卿二人，正四品，丞三人，正五品。

translations.literal: Two Vice Directors, rank 4a; three Assistants, rank 5a.
translations.idiomatic: There were two vice directors at rank 4a and three assistants at rank 5a.

sentences.zh: 其左、右寺官如故。

translations.literal: The officials of the Left and Right Sections remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right section staffs remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十九年又罷，盡移案牘於後湖。

translations.literal: Abolished again in the twenty-ninth year; all case documents were moved to Rear Lake.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished again in year 29 and all case files were moved to Rear Lake.

sentences.zh: 建文初復置，改左、右寺為司，寺正為都評事，寺副為副都評事，司務為都典簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen it was restored; the Left and Right Sections were changed to Offices, Section Directors to Chief Reviewing Officers, Section Vice Directors to Vice Chief Reviewing Officers, Secretariat Clerks to Chief Registry Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign it was restored: sections became offices, section directors chief reviewing officers, vice directors vice chiefs, and secretariat clerks chief registry clerks.

sentences.zh: 司務，洪武二十六年置。

translations.literal: Secretariat Clerks were established in the twenty-sixth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat clerk posts were created in Hongwu year 26.

sentences.zh: 成祖初，仍置大理寺，其左、右寺設官，復如洪武時。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengzu's reign the Court of Judicial Review was still established; its Left and Right Sections and appointed officials were restored as in the Hongwu period.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongle the court was re-established with left and right sections staffed as in the Hongwu era.

sentences.zh: 又因左、右二寺評事多寡不等，所治事亦繁簡不均，以二寺評事均分，左、右各六人，如刑部、都察院十二司道，各帶管直隸地方審錄。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the reviewing officers of the Left and Right Sections were unequal in number and the matters they handled were uneven in burden, the reviewing officers of the two sections were evenly divided, six each on left and right, like the twelve circuit offices of the Ministry of Justice and Censorate, each also overseeing review and recording in directly administered places.
translations.idiomatic: Because caseloads were uneven, reviewing officers were split evenly—six per section—like the twelve circuits of the Ministry of Justice and Censorate, each also handling review in the directly administered region.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖設左評事四員，分管在京諸司及直隸衛所、府州縣刑名。

translations.literal: At first Taizu established four Left Reviewing Officers, separately supervising criminal cases of offices in the capital and guards, prefectures, and counties of the directly administered region.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Taizu appointed four left reviewing officers for capital agencies and directly administered guards, prefectures, and counties.

sentences.zh: 右評事八員，分管在外十三布政司、都司、衛所、府州縣刑名。

translations.literal: Eight Right Reviewing Officers separately supervised criminal cases of the thirteen provincial administrations, regional commands, guards, battalions, prefectures, and counties outside [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: Eight right reviewing officers handled criminal cases in the thirteen provinces and their commands, guards, and local administrations.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，仍復舊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle the former arrangement was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 the earlier arrangement was restored.

sentences.zh: 後定都北京，又改分寺屬。

translations.literal: Later, when the capital was fixed at Beijing, the division of section jurisdictions was again changed.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was fixed at Beijing, section jurisdictions were redrawn.

sentences.zh: 兩京、五府、六部、京衛等衙門刑名，屬左寺。

translations.literal: Criminal cases of the two capitals, five prefectures, six ministries, capital guards, and other such offices belonged to the Left Section.
translations.idiomatic: The left section took cases from both capitals, the five prefectures, six ministries, and capital guards.

sentences.zh: 順天、應天二府，南、北直隸衛所、府州縣並在外浙江等布政司、都司、衛所刑名，屬右寺。

translations.literal: Shuntian and Yingtian prefectures, southern and northern directly administered guards, battalions, prefectures, and counties, together with criminal cases of provincial administrations such as Zhejiang outside [the capital], regional commands, and guards and battalions, belonged to the Right Section.
translations.idiomatic: The right section took Shuntian and Yingtian, north and south directly administered territory, and provincial cases including Zhejiang and other outer provinces.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，裁減右評事四人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi four Right Reviewing Officers were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1 four right reviewing officers were cut.

sentences.zh: 時天下罪囚，類不解審，右寺事顧簡於左寺。

translations.literal: At the time prisoners throughout the realm generally did not undergo review; the Right Section's business was plainly lighter than the Left Section's.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners empire-wide often went without review, and the right section's workload was noticeably lighter than the left's.

sentences.zh: 萬曆九年，更定左、右寺分理天下刑獄。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wanli the Left and Right Sections' division of handling penal cases throughout the realm was re-fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 9 the left and right sections' division of empire-wide criminal cases was redrawn.

sentences.zh: 浙江、福建、山東、廣東、四川、貴州六司道，左寺理之。

translations.literal: The six circuit offices of Zhejiang, Fujian, Shandong, Guangdong, Sichuan, and Guizhou were handled by the Left Section.
translations.idiomatic: The left section handled Zhejiang, Fujian, Shandong, Guangdong, Sichuan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 江西、陝西、河南、山西、湖廣、廣西、雲南七司道，右寺理之。

translations.literal: The seven circuit offices of Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Henan, Shanxi, Huguang, Guangxi, and Yunnan were handled by the Right Section.
translations.idiomatic: The right section handled Jiangxi, Shaanxi, Henan, Shanxi, Huguang, Guangxi, and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 以能按律出人罪者為稱職。

translations.literal: Those able according to statutes to release or convict according to guilt were deemed competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Competence meant sentencing strictly according to statute—convicting the guilty and freeing the innocent.

sentences.zh: 大理寺之設，為慎刑也。

translations.literal: The establishment of the Court of Judicial Review was for cautious application of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The court existed to ensure punishment was applied with caution.

sentences.zh: 三法司會審，初審，刑部、都察院為主，覆審，本寺為主。

translations.literal: In joint trial by the Three Judicial Offices, at initial review the Ministry of Justice and Censorate took the lead; at re-review this court took the lead.
translations.idiomatic: In joint trials by the three judicial offices, the Ministry of Justice and Censorate led the initial review and the court led the re-review.

sentences.zh: 明初，猶置刑具、牢獄。

translations.literal: In early Ming, penal instruments and prisons were still kept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty the court still kept instruments of punishment and its own prisons.

sentences.zh: 弘治以後，止閱案卷，囚徒俱不到寺。

translations.literal: After Hongzhi they only reviewed case documents; prisoners all did not come to the court.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzhi the court reviewed dossiers only; prisoners no longer appeared there.

sentences.zh: 司務典出納文移。

translations.literal: Secretariat Clerks managed receipt and dispatch of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerks handled incoming and outgoing paperwork.

sentences.zh: 詹事府 附左右春坊 司經局

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent; appended: Left and Right Eastern Palaces, Bureau for Classics of the Heir Apparent
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent; with appended sections on the Left and Right Eastern Palaces and the Bureau for Classics of the Heir Apparent

sentences.zh: 詹事府。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 詹事一人，正三品；

translations.literal: One Grand Mentor, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: One grand mentor, rank 3a;

sentences.zh: 少詹事二人，正四品；

translations.literal: two Deputy Grand Mentors, rank 4a;
translations.idiomatic: two deputy grand mentors, rank 4a;

sentences.zh: 府丞二人，正六品；

translations.literal: two Chancellors of the Household, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: two chancellors of the household, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 主簿廳，主簿一人，從七品；

translations.literal: a Registry, one Chief Clerk, rank 7b;
translations.idiomatic: a registry with one chief clerk, rank 7b;

sentences.zh: 錄事二人，正九品；

translations.literal: two Recording Clerks, rank 9a;
translations.idiomatic: two recording clerks, rank 9a;

sentences.zh: 通事舍人二人。

translations.literal: two Transmission Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: and two transmission attendants.

sentences.zh: 左春坊，大學士，正五品；

translations.literal: Left Eastern Palace: one Chief Instructor, rank 5a;
translations.idiomatic: Left Eastern Palace: one chief instructor, rank 5a;

sentences.zh: 左庶子，正五品；

translations.literal: Left Household Vice Prefect, rank 5a;
translations.idiomatic: left household vice prefect, rank 5a;

sentences.zh: 左諭德，從五品；

translations.literal: Left Preceptor, rank 5b;
translations.idiomatic: left preceptor, rank 5b;

sentences.zh: 各一人；

translations.literal: one each;
translations.idiomatic: one each;

sentences.zh: 左中允，正六品；

translations.literal: Left Palace Rectifier, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: left palace rectifier, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 左贊善，從六品；

translations.literal: Left Palace Supporter, rank 6b;
translations.idiomatic: left palace supporter, rank 6b;

sentences.zh: 左司直郎，從六品，後不常設；

translations.literal: Left Palace Direct Counselor, rank 6b, later not regularly established;
translations.idiomatic: left palace direct counselor, rank 6b, later not regularly filled;

sentences.zh: 各二人；

translations.literal: two each;
translations.idiomatic: two each;

sentences.zh: 左清紀郎一人，從八品，不常設；

translations.literal: one Left Records Regulator, rank 8b, not regularly established;
translations.idiomatic: one left records regulator, rank 8b, not regularly filled;

sentences.zh: 左司諫二人，從九品，不常設。

translations.literal: two Left Memorial Remonstrators, rank 9b, not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: two left memorial remonstrators, rank 9b, not regularly filled.

sentences.zh: 右春坊，亦如之。

translations.literal: The Right Eastern Palace was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The right eastern palace was organized the same way.

sentences.zh: 司經局，洗馬一人，從五品；

translations.literal: Bureau for Classics of the Heir Apparent: one Reader-in-Waiting, rank 5b;
translations.idiomatic: Bureau for Classics of the Heir Apparent: one reader-in-waiting, rank 5b;

sentences.zh: 校書，正九品；

translations.literal: Collators, rank 9a;
translations.idiomatic: collators, rank 9a;

sentences.zh: 正字，從九品；

translations.literal: Orthographers, rank 9b;
translations.idiomatic: orthographers, rank 9b;

sentences.zh: 各二人。

translations.literal: two each.
translations.idiomatic: two each.

sentences.zh: 詹事，掌統府、坊、局之政事，以輔導太子。

translations.literal: The Grand Mentor oversaw and unified the administrative affairs of the Secretariat, the eastern palaces, and the classics bureau, to assist and guide the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The grand mentor oversaw the Secretariat, the eastern palaces, and the classics bureau, guiding and instructing the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 少詹事佐之。

translations.literal: The Deputy Grand Mentor assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy grand mentor assisted him.

sentences.zh: 凡入侍太子，與坊、局翰林官番直進講《尚書》、《春秋》、《資治通鑒》、《大學衍義》、《貞觀政要》諸書。

translations.literal: All who entered attendance on the heir apparent, together with eastern-palace, classics-bureau, and Hanlin officials, took turns on duty lecturing on the Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign, and other such books.
translations.idiomatic: All who attended the heir apparent, together with officials of the eastern palaces, the classics bureau, and the Hanlin Academy, lectured in rotation on the Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign, and other such works.

sentences.zh: 前期纂輯成章進禦，然後赴文華殿講讀。

translations.literal: In advance they compiled and edited passages into chapters and presented them to the throne; only then did they go to the Wenhua Hall to lecture and read.
translations.idiomatic: They first compiled selected passages and presented them to the emperor, then went to the Wenhua Hall to lecture.

sentences.zh: 講讀畢，率其僚屬，以朝廷所處分軍國重事及撫諭諸蕃恩義，陳說於太子。

translations.literal: When the lecture and reading were finished, they led their subordinate officials and, taking the weighty military and state affairs decided by the court and the grace and righteousness with which the various frontier peoples were soothed and instructed, set them forth before the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the lecture, they led their staff to explain to the heir apparent the weighty military and civil decisions of the court and the principles by which the frontier peoples were reassured and governed.

sentences.zh: 凡朝賀，必先奏朝廷，乃具啟本以進。

translations.literal: For all court congratulations, they had first to memorialize the court; only then did they prepare a memorial of report and submit it.
translations.idiomatic: For all court congratulations, they first reported to the court, then prepared a formal memorial to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 凡府僚暨坊、局官與翰林院職互相兼，試士、修書皆與焉。

translations.literal: All secretariat staff together with eastern-palace and classics-bureau officials and Hanlin Academy posts were mutually held in concurrent appointment, and they all took part in examining candidates and compiling books.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat staff, eastern-palace and classics-bureau officials, and Hanlin posts were often held concurrently, and all took part in examinations and book compilation.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人，典東宮朝謁、辭見之禮，承令勞問之事，凡廷臣朝賀、進箋、進春、進曆於太子，則引入而舉案。

translations.literal: The Transmission Attendant managed the rites of the eastern palace for court audiences and farewell audiences, and carried out orders for comforting inquiries; whenever court ministers offered congratulations, submitted memorials, presented the spring almanac, or presented the calendar to the heir apparent, he introduced them and raised the document tray.
translations.idiomatic: The transmission attendant managed eastern-palace rites of audience and farewell, carried out comforting inquiries on command, and whenever court ministers offered congratulations, memorials, the spring almanac, or the calendar to the heir apparent, introduced them and presented the documents.

sentences.zh: 春坊大學士，掌太子上奏請、下啟箋及講讀之事，皆審慎而監省之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace Chief Instructor was in charge of the heir apparent's upward memorials and requests, downward reports and letters, and matters of lecture and reading, all of which he examined with care and supervised.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace chief instructor supervised the heir apparent's memorials, reports, and lectures, examining each with care.

sentences.zh: 庶子、諭德、中允、贊善各奉其職以從。

translations.literal: The household vice prefects, preceptors, palace rectifiers, and palace supporters each performed their duties and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The household vice prefects, preceptors, palace rectifiers, and palace supporters each performed their duties under him.

sentences.zh: 凡東宮監國、撫軍、出狩，及朝會出入，覆啟，畫諾，必審署以移詹事。

translations.literal: For all cases in which the eastern palace supervised the state, pacified armies, went out hunting, or attended assemblies and went in and out, as well as for returned reports and written approvals, they had to be carefully signed and then forwarded to the Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the heir apparent acted as regent, inspected armies, went hunting, or attended court, and for all returned reports and written approvals, they had to be carefully signed and forwarded to the grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 諸祥眚必啟告。

translations.literal: All auspicious signs and calamities had to be reported and announced.
translations.idiomatic: All auspicious signs and calamities had to be reported.

sentences.zh: 內外庶政可為規鑒者，隨事而贊諭。

translations.literal: For ordinary internal and external administration that could serve as models and mirrors, they admonished and instructed as the matter required.
translations.idiomatic: They offered timely admonition and instruction on civil affairs at court and beyond that could serve the heir apparent as examples.

sentences.zh: 伶人、僕禦有改變新聲、導逢非禮者，則陳古義，申典制，糾正而請斥遠之。

translations.literal: If actors, musicians, or attendants altered new tunes or led him into what was not according to ritual, they set forth ancient principles, declared the canonical regulations, corrected the offense, and requested that the offenders be driven away.
translations.idiomatic: If entertainers or attendants introduced improper music or led the heir apparent into impropriety, they cited ancient precedent and current regulations, corrected the offense, and asked that the offenders be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 司直、清紀郎，掌彈劾宮僚，糾舉職事。

translations.literal: The palace direct counselor and records regulator were in charge of impeaching eastern-palace officials and investigating their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The palace direct counselor and records regulator impeached eastern-palace officials and investigated their conduct of office.

sentences.zh: 文華殿講讀畢，諸臣班退，有獨留奏事及私謁者，則共糾之。

translations.literal: When the lecture and reading at the Wenhua Hall were finished and the various ministers withdrew in formation, if anyone remained alone to report affairs or paid a private visit, they jointly impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: After lectures at the Wenhua Hall, if any minister lingered alone to report affairs or paid a private visit, they jointly impeached him.

sentences.zh: 司諫，掌箴誨鑒戒，以拾遺補過。

translations.literal: The memorial remonstrator was in charge of admonition, instruction, and warnings as mirrors, to pick up what was omitted and repair what was flawed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial remonstrator offered admonition and warning, remedying omissions and correcting faults.

sentences.zh: 凡有啟事於東宮，與司直、清紀執筆紀令旨，規正其偽繆者。

translations.literal: For all matters reported to the eastern palace, together with the palace direct counselor and records regulator he took up the brush to record orders and instructions and to correct what was false or in error.
translations.idiomatic: For all matters reported to the eastern palace, he joined the palace direct counselor and records regulator in recording orders and correcting errors.

sentences.zh: 洗馬，掌經史子集、制典、圖書刊輯之事。

translations.literal: The reader-in-waiting was in charge of the classics, histories, masters, and collections, of statutes and ordinances, and of the editing and compilation of books and maps.
translations.idiomatic: The reader-in-waiting oversaw the classics, histories, statutes, maps, and book compilation.

sentences.zh: 立正本、副本、貯本以備進覽。

translations.literal: He established master copies, duplicate copies, and stored copies to prepare them for presentation and perusal.
translations.idiomatic: He maintained master, duplicate, and archival copies for presentation to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 凡天下圖冊上東宮者，皆受而藏之。

translations.literal: All maps and registers of the realm sent up to the eastern palace were received and stored.
translations.idiomatic: All maps and registers sent to the eastern palace were received and stored.

sentences.zh: 校書、正字，掌繕寫裝潢，詮其訛謬而調其音切，以佐洗馬。

translations.literal: Collators and orthographers were in charge of copying, binding, and ornamentation, explaining errors and adjusting pronunciation and tones, to assist the reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Collators and orthographers copied and bound texts, corrected errors, and adjusted pronunciation and tones to assist the reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 先是，洪武初，置大本堂，充古今圖籍其中，召四方名儒訓導太子、親王。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the beginning of the Hongwu reign, the Great Origin Hall was established, ancient and modern maps and registers were stocked within it, and famous Confucians from all quarters were summoned to instruct and guide the heir apparent and imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the beginning of Hongwu, the Great Origin Hall was established and stocked with ancient and modern books and maps, and renowned scholars from across the realm were summoned to instruct the heir apparent and imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 諸儒專經面授，分番夜直。

translations.literal: The various scholars lectured on their specialties face to face and took turns on night duty.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars lectured on their specialties in person and took turns on night duty.

sentences.zh: 已而太子居文華堂，諸儒迭班侍從，又選才俊之士入充伴讀，時時賜宴、賦詩，商榷今古，評論文學。

translations.literal: Thereafter the heir apparent resided in the Wenhua Hall; the various scholars took turns in attendance in rotation, and talented and outstanding men were also selected to enter service as companion readers; from time to time banquets and poetic compositions were bestowed, and they discussed past and present and commented on literature.
translations.idiomatic: Later the heir apparent moved to the Wenhua Hall; the scholars attended in rotation, and talented men were chosen as companion readers. They were often feasted and asked to compose verse, discussing past and present and debating literature.

sentences.zh: 是時東宮官屬，自太子少師、少傅、少保、賓客外，則有左、右詹事，同知詹事院事，副詹事，詹事丞，左、右率府使，同知左、右率府事，左、右率府副使，諭德，贊善大夫，皆以勳舊大臣兼領其職。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern-palace staff, apart from the heir apparent's junior tutor, junior mentor, junior guardian, and guest, included the left and right grand mentors, associate directors of the Grand Mentor Directorate, deputy grand mentors, grand-mentor assistants, left and right commandants of the guard office, associate commandants of the left and right guard offices, left and right deputy commandants of the guard office, preceptors, and grand masters of palace support — all of whom were concurrently led in their posts by meritorious old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, besides the heir apparent's junior tutors, mentors, guardian, and guest, the eastern palace had left and right grand mentors, deputy directors, assistants, guard commandants and their deputies, preceptors, and grand masters of palace support — all concurrently held by meritorious senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 又有文學、中舍、正字、侍正、洗馬、庶子及贊讀等官。

translations.literal: There were also the posts of literary officer, central secretary, orthographer, attendance director, reader-in-waiting, household vice prefect, and reading supporter.
translations.idiomatic: There were also literary officers, central secretaries, orthographers, attendance directors, readers-in-waiting, household vice prefects, and reading supporters.

sentences.zh: 十五年，更定左、右春坊官，各置庶子、諭德、中允、贊善、司直郎，又各設大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the offices of the left and right eastern palaces were redefined; each was given household vice prefects, preceptors, palace rectifiers, palace supporters, and palace direct counselors, and each also had a chief instructor established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the left and right eastern palaces were reorganized, each given household vice prefects, preceptors, palace rectifiers, palace supporters, and palace direct counselors, and each also given a chief instructor.

sentences.zh: 尋定司經局官，設洗馬、校書、正字。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the offices of the Bureau for Classics of the Heir Apparent were fixed, and reader-in-waiting, collator, and orthographer were established.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the classics bureau was organized with reader-in-waiting, collator, and orthographer.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以官聯無統，始置詹事院。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, because the chain of official posts lacked unified leadership, the Grand Mentor Directorate was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, because eastern-palace offices lacked unified leadership, the Grand Mentor Directorate was established.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，改院為府，定詹事秩正三品，春坊大學士正五品，司經局洗馬從五品。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the directorate was changed into a secretariat; the grand mentor's rank was fixed at 3a, the eastern palace chief instructor at 5a, and the reader-in-waiting of the classics bureau at 5b.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the directorate became a secretariat; the grand mentor was fixed at rank 3a, the eastern palace chief instructor at 5a, and the classics bureau reader-in-waiting at 5b.

sentences.zh: 雖各有印，而事總於詹事府。

translations.literal: Although each had its own seal, affairs were gathered under the Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Although each office had its own seal, affairs were centralized in the Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，增設左、右春坊清紀郎、司諫、通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year records regulators, memorial remonstrators, and transmission attendants were added to the left and right eastern palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year records regulators, memorial remonstrators, and transmission attendants were added to the left and right eastern palaces.

sentences.zh: 建文中，增少卿、寺丞各一人，賓客二人。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen reign one additional vice director and one directorate assistant were added, and two guests.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jianwen emperor one additional vice director and one directorate assistant were added, along with two guests.

sentences.zh: 又置資德院資德一人，資善二人。

translations.literal: The Virtue Resource Directorate was also established, with one virtue resource and two virtue supporters.
translations.idiomatic: A Virtue Resource Directorate was also established, with one virtue resource and two virtue supporters.

sentences.zh: 其屬，贊讀、贊書、著作郎各二人，掌典籍各一人。

translations.literal: Its subordinates were two reading supporters, two writing supporters, and two composition directors, and one archivist in charge of canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Its staff included two reading supporters, two writing supporters, two composition directors, and one archivist.

sentences.zh: 成祖復舊制。

translations.literal: The Chengzu emperor restored the old system.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzu emperor restored the old system.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，命大學士提調講讀官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yingzong reign, grand secretaries were ordered to take charge of and direct the lecture officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingzong reign, grand secretaries were ordered to supervise the lecture officials.

sentences.zh: 按詹事府多由他官兼掌。

translations.literal: According to the records, the Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent was for the most part concurrently directed by other officials.
translations.idiomatic: In practice the Grand Secretariat of the Heir Apparent was usually held concurrently by other officials.

sentences.zh: 天順以前，或尚書、侍郎、都御史，成化以後，率以禮部尚書、侍郎由翰林出身者兼掌之。

translations.literal: Before the Tianshun reign it might be a minister, vice minister, or censor-in-chief; after the Chenghua reign it was generally the minister or vice minister of rites who had risen from the Hanlin Academy who concurrently directed it.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tianshun it might be held by a ministry director, vice minister, or censor-in-chief; after Chenghua it was generally held by the minister or vice minister of rites, drawn from the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 其協理者無常員。

translations.literal: Its co-administrators had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Its co-administrators had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 春坊大學士，景泰間，倪謙、劉定之而後，僅楊廷和一任之，後不復設。

translations.literal: As for the eastern palace chief instructor, in the Jingtai period, after Ni Qian and Liu Dingzhi, only Yang Tinghe held the post once; afterward it was not established again.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace chief instructor, after Ni Qian and Liu Dingzhi in the Jingtai period, was held only once by Yang Tinghe and was never reestablished.

sentences.zh: 其司直、司諫、清紀郎亦不常置。

translations.literal: Its palace direct counselors, memorial remonstrators, and records regulators were also not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Its palace direct counselors, memorial remonstrators, and records regulators were also not regularly filled.

sentences.zh: 惟嘉靖十八年以陸深為詹事，崔銑為少詹事，王教、羅洪先、華察等為諭德、贊善、洗馬，皇甫涍、唐順之等為司直、司諫，皆天下名儒。

translations.literal: Only in the eighteenth year of the Jiajing reign was Lu Shen made grand mentor, Cui Rui deputy grand mentor, Wang Jiao, Luo Hongxian, Hua Cha, and others made preceptors, palace supporters, and readers-in-waiting, and Huangfu Qin, Tang Shunzhi, and others made palace direct counselors and memorial remonstrators — all were famous Confucians of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the eighteenth year of Jiajing were Lu Shen made grand mentor, Cui Rui deputy grand mentor, Wang Jiao, Luo Hongxian, Hua Cha, and others made preceptors, palace supporters, and readers-in-waiting, and Huangfu Qin, Tang Shunzhi, and others made palace direct counselors and memorial remonstrators — all renowned scholars of the realm.

sentences.zh: 自明初宋濂諸人後，宮僚莫盛於此。

translations.literal: Since Song Lian and the others at the beginning of the Ming, no eastern-palace staff had ever been so illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song Lian and his colleagues at the beginning of the dynasty, no eastern-palace staff had ever been so distinguished.

sentences.zh: 嗣是，出閣講讀，每點別員，本府坊局僅為翰林官遷轉之階。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when the heir apparent left the palace to receive lectures, special appointees were each time designated; the secretariat and its eastern palaces and classics bureau became merely steps in the promotion of Hanlin officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when the heir apparent left the palace for lectures, special appointees were named each time, and the secretariat and its eastern palaces and classics bureau became merely rungs on the Hanlin career ladder.

sentences.zh: 翰林院

translations.literal: Hanlin Academy
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academy

sentences.zh: 翰林院。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 學士一人，正五品侍讀學士、侍講學士各二人，並從五品侍讀、侍講各二人，並正六品《五經》博士九人，正八品，並世襲，別見。

translations.literal: One Academician, rank 5a; two Reader-in-chief Lecturers and two Expositor-in-chief Lecturers, all rank 5b; two Readers and two Expositors, all rank 6a; nine Doctors of the Five Classics, rank 8a, all hereditary — treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: One academician, rank 5a; two reader-in-chief lecturers and two expositor-in-chief lecturers, rank 5b; two readers and two expositors, rank 6a; nine doctors of the Five Classics, rank 8a, all hereditary — treated separately elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 典籍二人，從八品侍書二人，正九品，後不常設。

translations.literal: two Archivists, rank 8b; two Attendant Scribes, rank 9a — the latter were later not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Two archivists, rank 8b; two attendant scribes, rank 9a — the latter were later not regularly filled.

sentences.zh: 待詔六人，從九品，不常設。

translations.literal: six Awaiting Edict, rank 9b, not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Six awaiting edict, rank 9b, not regularly filled.

sentences.zh: 孔目一人，未入流史官修撰，從六品編修，正七品檢討，從七品庶起士，無定員。

translations.literal: One Registrar, unranked; Historiographical Compiler, rank 6b; Editor, rank 7a; Reviser, rank 7b; Palace Graduates, without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: One registrar, unranked; historiographical compiler, rank 6b; editor, rank 7a; reviser, rank 7b; palace graduates, without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 學士，掌制誥、史冊、文翰之事，以考議制度，詳正文書，備天子顧問。

translations.literal: The Academician was in charge of edicts, historical records, and literary documents, examining and deliberating on institutions, correcting and completing written documents, and serving as adviser to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The academician drafted edicts, managed historical records and documents, reviewed institutions, polished official writing, and advised the emperor.

sentences.zh: 凡經筵日講，纂修實錄、玉牒、史志諸書，編纂六曹章奏，皆奉敕而統承之。

translations.literal: For all daily lectures at the classics mat, compilation of veritable records, jade registers, historical annals, and other books, and editing of memorials from the six ministries, he received imperial command and took overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: Daily lectures at the classics mat, compilation of veritable records, jade registers, histories, and memorials from the six ministries all came under his direction by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 誥敕，以學士一人兼領。

translations.literal: Proclamations and commissions were concurrently led by one academician.
translations.idiomatic: Proclamations and commissions were concurrently directed by one academician.

sentences.zh: 正統中，王直、王英以禮部侍郎兼學士，專領誥敕，後罷。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong period Wang Zhi and Wang Ying, as vice ministers of rites concurrently holding academician rank, specially directed proclamations and commissions; the post was later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengtong, Wang Zhi and Wang Ying, as vice ministers of rites concurrently holding academician rank, were put in sole charge of proclamations and commissions; the arrangement was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年復設。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Hongzhi reign it was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: It was reestablished in the seventh year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 正德中，白鉞、費宏等由禮部尚書入東閣，專典誥敕。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period Bai Yue, Fei Hong, and others entered the Eastern Pavilion from the post of minister of rites and were put in sole charge of proclamations and commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, Bai Yue, Fei Hong, and others entered the Eastern Pavilion from the ministry of rites and were put in sole charge of proclamations and commissions.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年復罷，以講、讀、編、檢等官管之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Jiajing reign it was again abolished, and expositor, reader, editor, reviser, and other officials were put in charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished again in the sixth year of Jiajing, and expositors, readers, editors, revisers, and other officials took charge.

sentences.zh: 大政事、大典禮，集諸臣會議，則與諸司參決其可否。

translations.literal: For great state affairs and great ceremonial occasions, when the various ministers were gathered in conference, he joined the various offices in deliberating whether they should be approved or not.
translations.idiomatic: On great state affairs and great ceremonies, when ministers were gathered in conference, he joined the ministries in deciding what should be approved.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸太學聽講，凡郊祀慶成諸宴，則學士侍坐於四品京卿上。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the Imperial Academy to hear lectures, and for all banquets following suburban sacrifices and celebratory completions, the academician was seated in attendance above capital officials of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy to hear lectures, and at banquets following suburban sacrifices and celebratory rites, the academician was seated above capital officials of the fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 侍讀、侍講，掌講讀經史。

translations.literal: Readers and expositors were in charge of lecturing on and reading the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Readers and expositors lectured on the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 《五經》博士，初置五人，各掌專經講義，繼以優給聖賢先儒後裔世襲，不治院事。

translations.literal: The Doctors of the Five Classics were first established as five persons, each in charge of lecturing on his specialty classic; later they were given preferential treatment as hereditary descendants of the sages and former Confucians and did not administer academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The doctors of the Five Classics were first five in number, each lecturing on his specialty classic; later they were given preferential treatment as hereditary descendants of the sages and earlier Confucians and did not administer academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 史官，掌修國史。

translations.literal: Historiographical officers were in charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Historiographical officers compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 凡天文、地理、宗潢、禮樂、兵刑諸大政，及詔敕、書檄，批答王言，皆籍而記之，以備實錄。

translations.literal: All great policies concerning astronomy, geography, the imperial clan, ritual and music, military affairs and punishments, as well as edicts, commissions, letters and proclamations, and written replies to the kingly words, were all entered and recorded to prepare material for the veritable records.
translations.idiomatic: All major policies on astronomy, geography, the imperial clan, ritual, music, military affairs, and punishments, as well as edicts, letters, and written replies to imperial orders, were recorded for the veritable records.

sentences.zh: 國家有纂修著作之書，則分掌考輯撰述之事。

translations.literal: When the state had books to compile and edit, they divided responsibility for examining, compiling, and composing them.
translations.idiomatic: When the state undertook compilations, they divided responsibility for research, editing, and writing.

sentences.zh: 經筵充展卷官，鄉試充考試官，會試充同考官，殿試充收卷官。

translations.literal: At the classics mat they served as scroll-presenting officers; at the provincial examination as examining officers; at the metropolitan examination as associate examiners; and at the palace examination as receiving officers.
translations.idiomatic: At the classics mat they presented scrolls; at the provincial examination they served as examiners; at the metropolitan examination as associate examiners; and at the palace examination as receiving officers.

sentences.zh: 凡記注起居，編纂六曹章奏，謄黃冊封等咸充之。

translations.literal: For all recording of imperial movements and rest, editing of memorials from the six ministries, transcription in yellow for sealing, and the like, they all took part.
translations.idiomatic: They also recorded the emperor's movements, edited memorials from the six ministries, and copied documents for sealing.

sentences.zh: 庶起士，讀書翰林院，以學士一人教習之。

translations.literal: Palace graduates studied in the Hanlin Academy, and one academician instructed them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace graduates studied in the Hanlin Academy under the instruction of one academician.

sentences.zh: 侍書，掌以六書供侍。

translations.literal: Attendant scribes were in charge of attending with the six scripts.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant scribes attended with the six scripts.

sentences.zh: 待詔，掌應對。

translations.literal: Awaiting edict officers were in charge of responding to commands.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting edict officers responded to commands.

sentences.zh: 孔目掌文移。

translations.literal: The registrar was in charge of documents and communications.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar managed documents and communications.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，初置翰林院，秩正三品，設學士，正三品侍講學士，正四品直學士，正五品修撰、典簿，正七品編修，正八品洪武二年，置學士承旨，正三品，改學士，從三品。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu the Hanlin Academy was first established, rank 3a; an Academician was established, rank 3a; an Expositor-in-chief Lecturer, rank 4a; a Direct Academician, rank 5a; a Compiler and Registrar, rank 7a; an Editor, rank 8a. In the second year of Hongwu the Academician as Proclaimer was established, rank 3a; the Academician was changed to rank 3b.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wu the Hanlin Academy was established at rank 3a, with an academician at 3a, an expositor-in-chief lecturer at 4a, a direct academician at 5a, a compiler and registrar at 7a, and an editor at 8a. In the second year of Hongwu an academician proclaimer was added at 3a, and the academician was reduced to 3b.

sentences.zh: 侍講學士，正四品，侍讀學士，從四品，修撰，正六品。

translations.literal: Expositor-in-chief Lecturer, rank 4a; Reader-in-chief Lecturer, rank 4b; Compiler, rank 6a.
translations.idiomatic: Expositor-in-chief lecturer, rank 4a; reader-in-chief lecturer, rank 4b; compiler, rank 6a.

sentences.zh: 增設待制，從五品應奉，正七品典籍從八品等官。

translations.literal: Awaiting Composition, rank 5b; Responding Attendant, rank 7a; Archivist, rank 8b, and other such offices were added.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting composition, rank 5b; responding attendant, rank 7a; archivist, rank 8b, and other such offices were added.

sentences.zh: 十三年，增設檢閱，從九品。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Reviewer was added, rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year a reviewer was added at rank 9b.

sentences.zh: 十四年，定學士為正五品，革承旨、直學士、待制、應奉、檢閱、典簿，設孔目、《五經》博士、侍書、待詔、檢討。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Academician was fixed at rank 5a; Proclaimer, Direct Academician, Awaiting Composition, Responding Attendant, Reviewer, and Registrar were abolished; Registrar, Doctors of the Five Classics, Attendant Scribe, Awaiting Edict, and Reviser were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the academician was fixed at rank 5a; the proclaimer, direct academician, awaiting composition, responding attendant, reviewer, and registrar were abolished; and registrar, doctors of the Five Classics, attendant scribe, awaiting edict, and reviser were established.

sentences.zh: 令編修、檢討、典籍同左春坊左司直郎、正字、贊讀考駁諸司奏啟，平允則署其銜曰：「翰林院兼平駁諸司文章事某官某」，列名書之。

translations.literal: Editors, revisers, and archivists were ordered, together with the left palace direct counselor, orthographer, and reading supporter of the left eastern palace, to examine and judge the memorials and reports of the various offices; if fair and fitting, they signed with the title "Such-and-such official of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently judging the documents of the various offices," and wrote their names in a list.
